Also use for managing checkpoints, restores, and understanding network policy in the Sprite VM.
- sprite-api-gateway: Use this skill when users want to access external APIs (GitHub, Slack, Linear, etc.), integrate with third-party services, or need authenticated API calls. The API gateway at api.sprites.dev handles authentication automatically — sprites never need raw API keys or tokens.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".

Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.

# Sprite Environment

## CRITICAL: Security Rules
- HTTP services you create may become PUBLIC - never expose secrets, env vars, or sensitive data
- See /.sprite/docs/agent-context.md for full security requirements

## Quick Reference

### URL
- Format: `https://<sprite-name>-<org>.sprites.dev/`
- Check yours: `sprite-env info` or `sprite url` (from outside)
- Auth modes: `sprite` (org members only, default) or `public` (open to internet)
- Proxy routes HTTP to the service with `--http-port`, or port 8080 by default

### Services
- Long-running processes that persist across reboots
- Create: `sprite-env services create <name> --cmd <command> [--http-port <port>]`
- Only one service can have `--http-port`; it auto-starts on incoming requests
- `--cmd` takes the binary only; pass arguments via `--args`: `--cmd python3 --args "-m,http.server,8080"`
- Do NOT start a background process separately — the service manages the process lifecycle
- Restart: `sprite-env services restart <name>` (do NOT use stop + start separately)
- List/start/stop/delete: `sprite-env services <subcommand>`
- Full help: `sprite-env services --help`

### Checkpoints
- Point-in-time snapshots of the writable filesystem overlay
- Create before risky changes, restore to roll back
- CLI: `sprite-env checkpoints create`, `sprite-env checkpoints list`

### Lifecycle
- Sprites run while servicing HTTP requests or while sessions generate output
- When idle, sprites pause automatically
- Services and sessions keep sprites alive
- Services restart automatically on boot

### Directory Layout
```
/.sprite/
  bin/              # sprite-env CLI — use this to manage services and checkpoints
  docs/             # Documentation (agent-context.md, languages.md)
  checkpoints/      # Last 5 checkpoints mounted here
  policy/           # Network egress policy (network.json)
  languages/        # Per-language llm.txt files
```

## Full Documentation

- /.sprite/docs/agent-context.md - Environment overview (URL, services, checkpoints, network policy)
- /.sprite/docs/languages.md     - Language runtimes and version managers

Per-language details: /.sprite/languages/<lang>/llm.txt

CLI help: `sprite-env --help`

[package]
name = "type"
version = "0.1.0"
description = "A Tauri App"
authors = ["you"]
edition = "2021"

# See more keys and their definitions at https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/manifest.html

[lib]
# The `_lib` suffix may seem redundant but it is necessary
# to make the lib name unique and wouldn't conflict with the bin name.
# This seems to be only an issue on Windows, see https://github.com/rust-lang/cargo/issues/8519
name = "notes_reviewer_lib"
crate-type = ["staticlib", "cdylib", "rlib"]

[build-dependencies]
tauri-build = { version = "2", features = [] }

[dependencies]
tauri = { version = "2", features = ["macos-private-api"] }
tauri-plugin-opener = "2"
serde = { version = "1", features = ["derive"] }
serde_json = "1"
tauri-plugin-dialog = "2"
git2 = { version = "0.20", features = ["vendored-openssl"] }
base64 = "0.22"
reqwest = { version = "0.12", default-features = false, features = ["blocking", "json", "rustls-tls"] }
uuid = { version = "1", features = ["v7"] }
time = { version = "0.3", features = ["formatting", "macros", "parsing"] }
tauri-plugin-deep-link = "2"
tauri-plugin-ota = { git = "https://github.com/inkibra/tauri-plugins", tag = "@inkibra/tauri-plugin-ota@0.1.3", package = "tauri-plugin-ota" }
argon2 = "0.5"
chacha20poly1305 = { version = "0.10", features = ["std"] }
zeroize = "1.8"
zip = { version = "0.6", default-features = false, features = ["deflate"] }
mdns-sd = "0.20.0"

# Desktop-only auto-updater. The updater + process plugins are not built for
# mobile (iOS/Android), so they are gated to desktop targets here and behind
# `#[cfg(desktop)]` in commands/mod.rs.
[target.'cfg(not(any(target_os = "android", target_os = "ios")))'.dependencies]
tauri-plugin-updater = "2"
tauri-plugin-process = "2"

[target.'cfg(target_os = "macos")'.dependencies]
objc = "0.2"

[target.'cfg(target_os = "ios")'.dependencies]
objc = "0.2"

name: CI

# Fast feedback on every PR and on pushes to the default branch: typecheck +
# unit tests for both the React frontend and the Rust backend. Release/build
# workflows live in release.yml and deploy-pages.yml.
on:
  push:
    branches: [main, master]
  pull_request:

jobs:
  frontend:
    name: Frontend (typecheck + vitest)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20
          cache: npm
      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm install
      - name: Typecheck
        run: npx tsc --noEmit
      - name: Unit tests
        run: npm test

  backend:
    name: Backend (cargo test)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
      - uses: swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        with:
          workspaces: src-tauri
      # Tauri's Linux build needs these system libraries to compile the lib
      # (and therefore its test harness).
      - name: Install Linux build dependencies
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y \
            libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev \
            libgtk-3-dev \
            libayatana-appindicator3-dev \
            librsvg2-dev \
            patchelf
      - name: Rust unit tests
        run: cargo test --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml --lib

content.content:
1	name: Release
2	
3	# Tag-driven releases. The tag encodes both the version and which platform(s) to
4	# ship:
5	#   v1.2.3           -> desktop (.dmg + updater) AND iOS (App Store)
6	#   v1.2.3-desktop   -> desktop only
7	#   v1.2.3-ios       -> iOS only
8	#
9	# You can also trigger manually from the Actions tab (workflow_dispatch) and pick
10	# the version + platforms there — handy for re-running a build without a new tag.
11	on:
12	  push:
13	    tags:
14	      - "v*"
15	  workflow_dispatch:
16	    inputs:
17	      version:
18	        description: "Version to release, e.g. 1.2.3"
19	        required: true
20	        type: string
21	      platforms:
22	        description: "Which platforms to build"
23	        required: true
24	        default: "both"
25	        type: choice
26	        options: [both, desktop, ios]
27	
28	jobs:
29	  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
30	  # Parse the tag (or manual inputs) into a version + per-platform booleans.
31	  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
32	  setup:
33	    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
34	    outputs:
35	      version: ${{ steps.parse.outputs.version }}
36	      tag: ${{ steps.parse.outputs.tag }}
37	      desktop: ${{ steps.parse.outputs.desktop }}
38	      ios: ${{ steps.parse.outputs.ios }}
39	    steps:
40	      - id: parse
41	        run: |
42	          set -e
43	          if [ "${{ github.event_name }}" = "workflow_dispatch" ]; then
44	            VERSION="${{ inputs.version }}"
45	            SEL="${{ inputs.platforms }}"
46	            TAG="v$VERSION"
47	          else
48	            TAG="${{ github.ref_name }}"          # e.g. v1.2.3-ios
49	            BASE="${TAG#v}"                        # strip leading v
50	            case "$BASE" in
51	              *-ios)     VERSION="${BASE%-ios}";     SEL="ios" ;;
52	              *-desktop) VERSION="${BASE%-desktop}"; SEL="desktop" ;;
53	              *)         VERSION="$BASE";            SEL="both" ;;
54	            esac
55	          fi
56	
57	          DESKTOP=false; IOS=false
58	          case "$SEL" in
59	            both)    DESKTOP=true; IOS=true ;;
60	            desktop) DESKTOP=true ;;
61	            ios)     IOS=true ;;
62	            *) echo "Unknown platform selection: $SEL" >&2; exit 1 ;;
63	          esac
64	
65	          {
66	            echo "version=$VERSION"
67	            echo "tag=$TAG"
68	            echo "desktop=$DESKTOP"
69	            echo "ios=$IOS"
70	          } >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
71	          echo "Release -> version=$VERSION tag=$TAG desktop=$DESKTOP ios=$IOS"
72	
73	  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
74	  # Desktop (macOS): .dmg + updater artifacts, published as a GitHub Release.
75	  # tauri-action builds, signs the updater payload, generates latest.json, and
76	  # uploads everything to the release for this tag.
77	  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
78	  desktop:
79	    needs: setup
80	    if: needs.setup.outputs.desktop == 'true'
81	    runs-on: macos-latest
82	    permissions:
83	      contents: write
84	    steps:
85	      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
86	
87	      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
88	        with:
89	          node-version: 20
90	          cache: npm
91	
92	      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
93	      - uses: swatinem/rust-cache@v2
94	        with:
95	          workspaces: src-tauri
96	
97	      - name: Install dependencies
98	        run: npm install
99	
100	      - name: Set app version from tag
101	        run: bash scripts/set-app-version.sh "${{ needs.setup.outputs.version }}"
102	
103	      - name: Build, sign & publish desktop release
104	        uses: tauri-apps/tauri-action@v0
105	        env:
106	          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
107	          # Updater signing (required) — see docs/RELEASING.md.
108	          TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY: ${{ secrets.TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY }}
109	          TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD }}
110	          # Apple notarization (optional — removes the Gatekeeper warning). Leave
111	          # unset to ship an unsigned .dmg (right-click → Open to launch).
112	          APPLE_CERTIFICATE: ${{ secrets.APPLE_CERTIFICATE }}
113	          APPLE_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.APPLE_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD }}
114	          APPLE_SIGNING_IDENTITY: ${{ secrets.APPLE_SIGNING_IDENTITY }}
115	          APPLE_ID: ${{ secrets.APPLE_ID }}
116	          APPLE_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.APPLE_PASSWORD }}
117	          APPLE_TEAM_ID: ${{ secrets.APPLE_TEAM_ID }}
118	        with:
119	          tagName: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.tag }}
120	          releaseName: "Type ${{ needs.setup.outputs.tag }}"
121	          releaseBody: "Automated desktop release. Download the .dmg below; existing installs update in-app via Settings → Updates."
122	          releaseDraft: false
123	          prerelease: false
124	          # Apple Silicon build. For Intel/universal, add --target universal-apple-darwin
125	          # and a matching darwin-x86_64 entry (tauri-action handles latest.json).
126	          args: --bundles app,dmg
127	
128	      # The desktop updater endpoint reads .../releases/latest/download/latest.json,
129	      # so the desktop release must be GitHub's "latest". A `-desktop` tag is
130	      # semver-prerelease syntax, so force the flag to be safe. (iOS-only releases
131	      # are NOT marked latest, so they never hijack the desktop update channel.)
132	      - name: Mark release as latest
133	        env:
134	          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
135	        run: gh release edit "${{ needs.setup.outputs.tag }}" --latest --prerelease=false
136	
137	  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
138	  # iOS: native App Store build. Requires Apple signing assets as repo secrets
139	  # (see docs/RELEASING.md → "iOS CI setup"). This is the native binary path;
140	  # JS-only changes ship faster via the OTA bundle (deploy-pages.yml on main).
141	  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
142	  ios:
143	    needs: setup
144	    if: needs.setup.outputs.ios == 'true'
145	    runs-on: macos-latest
146	    steps:
147	      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
148	
149	      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
150	        with:
151	          node-version: 20
152	          cache: npm
153	
154	      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
155	        with:
156	          targets: aarch64-apple-ios
157	      - uses: swatinem/rust-cache@v2
158	        with:
159	          workspaces: src-tauri
160	
161	      - name: Install dependencies
162	        run: npm install
163	
164	      - name: Set app version from tag
165	        run: bash scripts/set-app-version.sh "${{ needs.setup.outputs.version }}"
166	
167	      # Give every App Store upload a unique build number (CFBundleVersion).
168	      - name: Set build number
169	        run: echo "TAURI_IOS_BUILD_NUMBER=${{ github.run_number }}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
170	
171	      - name: Import signing certificate
172	        uses: apple-actions/import-codesign-certs@v3
173	        with:
174	          p12-file-base64: ${{ secrets.APPLE_IOS_CERTIFICATE_P12 }}
175	          p12-password: ${{ secrets.APPLE_IOS_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD }}
176	
177	      - name: Install provisioning profile
178	        env:
179	          PROFILE_BASE64: ${{ secrets.APPLE_IOS_PROVISIONING_PROFILE }}
180	        run: |
181	          mkdir -p "$HOME/Library/MobileDevice/Provisioning Profiles"
182	          echo "$PROFILE_BASE64" | base64 --decode \
183	            > "$HOME/Library/MobileDevice/Provisioning Profiles/build.mobileprovision"
184	
185	      - name: Write App Store Connect API key
186	        env:
187	          ASC_KEY_BASE64: ${{ secrets.APPLE_ASC_API_KEY_P8 }}
188	          ASC_KEY_ID: ${{ secrets.APPLE_ASC_API_KEY_ID }}
189	        run: |
190	          mkdir -p private_keys
191	          echo "$ASC_KEY_BASE64" | base64 --decode > "private_keys/AuthKey_${ASC_KEY_ID}.p8"
192	
193	      - name: Initialize iOS project
194	        run: npm run tauri ios init
195	
196	      - name: Build iOS app (App Store export)
197	        run: npm run ios:build

file.content:
name: Release

# Tag-driven releases. The tag encodes both the version and which platform(s) to
# ship:
#   v1.2.3           -> desktop (.dmg + updater) AND iOS (App Store)
#   v1.2.3-desktop   -> desktop only
#   v1.2.3-ios       -> iOS only
#
# You can also trigger manually from the Actions tab (workflow_dispatch) and pick
# the version + platforms there — handy for re-running a build without a new tag.
on:
  push:
    tags:
      - "v*"
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      version:
        description: "Version to release, e.g. 1.2.3"
        required: true
        type: string
      platforms:
        description: "Which platforms to build"
        required: true
        default: "both"
        type: choice
        options: [both, desktop, ios]

jobs:
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Parse the tag (or manual inputs) into a version + per-platform booleans.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  setup:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      version: ${{ steps.parse.outputs.version }}
      tag: ${{ steps.parse.outputs.tag }}
      desktop: ${{ steps.parse.outputs.desktop }}
      ios: ${{ steps.parse.outputs.ios }}
    steps:
      - id: parse
        run: |
          set -e
          if [ "${{ github.event_name }}" = "workflow_dispatch" ]; then
            VERSION="${{ inputs.version }}"
            SEL="${{ inputs.platforms }}"
            TAG="v$VERSION"
          else
            TAG="${{ github.ref_name }}"          # e.g. v1.2.3-ios
            BASE="${TAG#v}"                        # strip leading v
            case "$BASE" in
              *-ios)     VERSION="${BASE%-ios}";     SEL="ios" ;;
              *-desktop) VERSION="${BASE%-desktop}"; SEL="desktop" ;;
              *)         VERSION="$BASE";            SEL="both" ;;
            esac
          fi

          DESKTOP=false; IOS=false
          case "$SEL" in
            both)    DESKTOP=true; IOS=true ;;
            desktop) DESKTOP=true ;;
            ios)     IOS=true ;;
            *) echo "Unknown platform selection: $SEL" >&2; exit 1 ;;
          esac

          {
            echo "version=$VERSION"
            echo "tag=$TAG"
            echo "desktop=$DESKTOP"
            echo "ios=$IOS"
          } >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "Release -> version=$VERSION tag=$TAG desktop=$DESKTOP ios=$IOS"

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Desktop (macOS): .dmg + updater artifacts, published as a GitHub Release.
  # tauri-action builds, signs the updater payload, generates latest.json, and
  # uploads everything to the release for this tag.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  desktop:
    needs: setup
    if: needs.setup.outputs.desktop == 'true'
    runs-on: macos-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20
          cache: npm

      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
      - uses: swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        with:
          workspaces: src-tauri

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm install

      - name: Set app version from tag
        run: bash scripts/set-app-version.sh "${{ needs.setup.outputs.version }}"

      - name: Build, sign & publish desktop release
        uses: tauri-apps/tauri-action@v0
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          # Updater signing (required) — see docs/RELEASING.md.
          TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY: ${{ secrets.TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD }}
          # Apple notarization (optional — removes the Gatekeeper warning). Leave
          # unset to ship an unsigned .dmg (right-click → Open to launch).
          APPLE_CERTIFICATE: ${{ secrets.APPLE_CERTIFICATE }}
          APPLE_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.APPLE_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD }}
          APPLE_SIGNING_IDENTITY: ${{ secrets.APPLE_SIGNING_IDENTITY }}
          APPLE_ID: ${{ secrets.APPLE_ID }}
          APPLE_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.APPLE_PASSWORD }}
          APPLE_TEAM_ID: ${{ secrets.APPLE_TEAM_ID }}
        with:
          tagName: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.tag }}
          releaseName: "Type ${{ needs.setup.outputs.tag }}"
          releaseBody: "Automated desktop release. Download the .dmg below; existing installs update in-app via Settings → Updates."
          releaseDraft: false
          prerelease: false
          # Apple Silicon build. For Intel/universal, add --target universal-apple-darwin
          # and a matching darwin-x86_64 entry (tauri-action handles latest.json).
          args: --bundles app,dmg

      # The desktop updater endpoint reads .../releases/latest/download/latest.json,
      # so the desktop release must be GitHub's "latest". A `-desktop` tag is
      # semver-prerelease syntax, so force the flag to be safe. (iOS-only releases
      # are NOT marked latest, so they never hijack the desktop update channel.)
      - name: Mark release as latest
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: gh release edit "${{ needs.setup.outputs.tag }}" --latest --prerelease=false

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # iOS: native App Store build. Requires Apple signing assets as repo secrets
  # (see docs/RELEASING.md → "iOS CI setup"). This is the native binary path;
  # JS-only changes ship faster via the OTA bundle (deploy-pages.yml on main).
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  ios:
    needs: setup
    if: needs.setup.outputs.ios == 'true'
    runs-on: macos-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20
          cache: npm

      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
        with:
          targets: aarch64-apple-ios
      - uses: swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        with:
          workspaces: src-tauri

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm install

      - name: Set app version from tag
        run: bash scripts/set-app-version.sh "${{ needs.setup.outputs.version }}"

      # Give every App Store upload a unique build number (CFBundleVersion).
      - name: Set build number
        run: echo "TAURI_IOS_BUILD_NUMBER=${{ github.run_number }}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

      - name: Import signing certificate
        uses: apple-actions/import-codesign-certs@v3
        with:
          p12-file-base64: ${{ secrets.APPLE_IOS_CERTIFICATE_P12 }}
          p12-password: ${{ secrets.APPLE_IOS_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD }}

      - name: Install provisioning profile
        env:
          PROFILE_BASE64: ${{ secrets.APPLE_IOS_PROVISIONING_PROFILE }}
        run: |
          mkdir -p "$HOME/Library/MobileDevice/Provisioning Profiles"
          echo "$PROFILE_BASE64" | base64 --decode \
            > "$HOME/Library/MobileDevice/Provisioning Profiles/build.mobileprovision"

      - name: Write App Store Connect API key
        env:
          ASC_KEY_BASE64: ${{ secrets.APPLE_ASC_API_KEY_P8 }}
          ASC_KEY_ID: ${{ secrets.APPLE_ASC_API_KEY_ID }}
        run: |
          mkdir -p private_keys
          echo "$ASC_KEY_BASE64" | base64 --decode > "private_keys/AuthKey_${ASC_KEY_ID}.p8"

      - name: Initialize iOS project
        run: npm run tauri ios init

      - name: Build iOS app (App Store export)
        run: npm run ios:build

      - name: Upload to App Store Connect
        env:
          ASC_KEY_ID: ${{ secrets.APPLE_ASC_API_KEY_ID }}
          ASC_ISSUER_ID: ${{ secrets.APPLE_ASC_API_ISSUER_ID }}
        run: |
          IPA=$(find src-tauri/gen/apple/build -name "*.ipa" | head -1)
          echo "Uploading $IPA"
          xcrun altool --upload-app --type ios --file "$IPA" \
            --apiKey "$ASC_KEY_ID" --apiIssuer "$ASC_ISSUER_ID"

file.content:
name: Deploy GitHub Pages

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
      - master
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read
  pages: write
  id-token: write

concurrency:
  group: pages
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Setup Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20
          cache: npm

      - name: Configure Pages
        uses: actions/configure-pages@v5

      - name: Resolve Pages URLs
        run: |
          OWNER="${{ github.repository_owner }}"
          REPO="${{ github.event.repository.name }}"

          if [ "$REPO" = "$OWNER.github.io" ]; then
            BASE_PATH="/"
            REPO_PREFIX=""
          else
            BASE_PATH="/$REPO/"
            REPO_PREFIX="/$REPO"
          fi

          SITE_URL="https://$OWNER.github.io$REPO_PREFIX"
          OTA_MANIFEST_URL="$SITE_URL/ota/manifest.json"
          OTA_CDN_BASE_URL="$SITE_URL/ota"

          echo "BASE_PATH=$BASE_PATH" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          echo "VITE_OTA_MANIFEST_URL=$OTA_MANIFEST_URL" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          echo "OTA_CDN_BASE_URL=$OTA_CDN_BASE_URL" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm install

      - name: Build web + OTA artifacts
        run: |
          npx tsc
          npx vite build --base "$BASE_PATH"
          npx vite build --config vite.ota.config.ts --base "$BASE_PATH"
          npm run ota:prepare
          touch dist/.nojekyll

      - name: Upload Pages artifact
        uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@v3
        with:
          path: dist

  deploy:
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment:
      name: github-pages
      url: ${{ steps.deployment.outputs.page_url }}
    steps:
      - name: Deploy to GitHub Pages
        id: deployment
        uses: actions/deploy-pages@v4

name: CI

# Fast feedback on every PR and on pushes to the default branch: typecheck +
# unit tests for every npm workspace (desktop app, shared packages, mobile app)
# and the Rust cargo workspace (core crates + Tauri backend). Release/build
# workflows live in release.yml and deploy-pages.yml.
on:
  push:
    branches: [main, master]
  pull_request:

jobs:
  typescript:
    name: TypeScript (typecheck + tests, all workspaces)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 22
          cache: npm
      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm install
      - name: Typecheck
        run: npm run typecheck --workspaces --if-present
      - name: Unit tests
        run: npm test --workspaces --if-present

  rust:
    name: Rust (cargo test, workspace)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
      - uses: swatinem/rust-cache@v2
      # Tauri's Linux build needs these system libraries to compile the lib
      # (and therefore its test harness).
      - name: Install Linux build dependencies
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y \
            libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev \
            libgtk-3-dev \
            libayatana-appindicator3-dev \
            librsvg2-dev \
            patchelf
      - name: Rust unit tests
        run: cargo test --workspace --lib

name: Release

# Tag-driven releases. The tag encodes both the version and which platform(s) to
# ship:
#   v1.2.3           -> desktop (.dmg + updater) AND iOS (App Store)
#   v1.2.3-desktop   -> desktop only
#   v1.2.3-ios       -> iOS only
#
# You can also trigger manually from the Actions tab (workflow_dispatch) and pick
# the version + platforms there — handy for re-running a build without a new tag.
on:
  push:
    tags:
      - "v*"
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      version:
        description: "Version to release, e.g. 1.2.3"
        required: true
        type: string
      platforms:
        description: "Which platforms to build"
        required: true
        default: "both"
        type: choice
        options: [both, desktop, ios]

jobs:
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Parse the tag (or manual inputs) into a version + per-platform booleans.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  setup:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      version: ${{ steps.parse.outputs.version }}
      tag: ${{ steps.parse.outputs.tag }}
      desktop: ${{ steps.parse.outputs.desktop }}
      ios: ${{ steps.parse.outputs.ios }}
    steps:
      - id: parse
        run: |
          set -e
          if [ "${{ github.event_name }}" = "workflow_dispatch" ]; then
            VERSION="${{ inputs.version }}"
            SEL="${{ inputs.platforms }}"
            TAG="v$VERSION"
          else
            TAG="${{ github.ref_name }}"          # e.g. v1.2.3-ios
            BASE="${TAG#v}"                        # strip leading v
            case "$BASE" in
              *-ios)     VERSION="${BASE%-ios}";     SEL="ios" ;;
              *-desktop) VERSION="${BASE%-desktop}"; SEL="desktop" ;;
              *)         VERSION="$BASE";            SEL="both" ;;
            esac
          fi

          DESKTOP=false; IOS=false
          case "$SEL" in
            both)    DESKTOP=true; IOS=true ;;
            desktop) DESKTOP=true ;;
            ios)     IOS=true ;;
            *) echo "Unknown platform selection: $SEL" >&2; exit 1 ;;
          esac

          {
            echo "version=$VERSION"
            echo "tag=$TAG"
            echo "desktop=$DESKTOP"
            echo "ios=$IOS"
          } >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "Release -> version=$VERSION tag=$TAG desktop=$DESKTOP ios=$IOS"

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Desktop (macOS): .dmg + updater artifacts, published as a GitHub Release.
  # tauri-action builds, signs the updater payload, generates latest.json, and
  # uploads everything to the release for this tag.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  desktop:
    needs: setup
    if: needs.setup.outputs.desktop == 'true'
    runs-on: macos-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20
          cache: npm

      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
      - uses: swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        with:
          workspaces: src-tauri

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm install

      - name: Set app version from tag
        run: bash scripts/set-app-version.sh "${{ needs.setup.outputs.version }}"

      - name: Build, sign & publish desktop release
        uses: tauri-apps/tauri-action@v0
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          # Updater signing (required) — see docs/RELEASING.md.
          TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY: ${{ secrets.TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD }}
          # Apple notarization (optional — removes the Gatekeeper warning). Leave
          # unset to ship an unsigned .dmg (right-click → Open to launch).
          APPLE_CERTIFICATE: ${{ secrets.APPLE_CERTIFICATE }}
          APPLE_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.APPLE_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD }}
          APPLE_SIGNING_IDENTITY: ${{ secrets.APPLE_SIGNING_IDENTITY }}
          APPLE_ID: ${{ secrets.APPLE_ID }}
          APPLE_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.APPLE_PASSWORD }}
          APPLE_TEAM_ID: ${{ secrets.APPLE_TEAM_ID }}
        with:
          tagName: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.tag }}
          releaseName: "Type ${{ needs.setup.outputs.tag }}"
          releaseBody: "Automated desktop release. Download the .dmg below; existing installs update in-app via Settings → Updates."
          releaseDraft: false
          prerelease: false
          # Apple Silicon build. For Intel/universal, add --target universal-apple-darwin
          # and a matching darwin-x86_64 entry (tauri-action handles latest.json).
          args: --bundles app,dmg

      # The desktop updater endpoint reads .../releases/latest/download/latest.json,
      # so the desktop release must be GitHub's "latest". A `-desktop` tag is
      # semver-prerelease syntax, so force the flag to be safe. (iOS-only releases
      # are NOT marked latest, so they never hijack the desktop update channel.)
      - name: Mark release as latest
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: gh release edit "${{ needs.setup.outputs.tag }}" --latest --prerelease=false

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # iOS: native App Store build. Requires Apple signing assets as repo secrets
  # (see docs/RELEASING.md → "iOS CI setup"). This is the native binary path;
  # JS-only changes ship faster via the OTA bundle (deploy-pages.yml on main).
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  ios:
    needs: setup
    if: needs.setup.outputs.ios == 'true'
    runs-on: macos-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20
          cache: npm

      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
        with:
          targets: aarch64-apple-ios
      - uses: swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        with:
          workspaces: src-tauri

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm install

      - name: Set app version from tag
        run: bash scripts/set-app-version.sh "${{ needs.setup.outputs.version }}"

      # Give every App Store upload a unique build number (CFBundleVersion).
      - name: Set build number
        run: echo "TAURI_IOS_BUILD_NUMBER=${{ github.run_number }}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

      - name: Import signing certificate
        uses: apple-actions/import-codesign-certs@v3
        with:
          p12-file-base64: ${{ secrets.APPLE_IOS_CERTIFICATE_P12 }}
          p12-password: ${{ secrets.APPLE_IOS_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD }}

      - name: Install provisioning profile
        env:
          PROFILE_BASE64: ${{ secrets.APPLE_IOS_PROVISIONING_PROFILE }}
        run: |
          mkdir -p "$HOME/Library/MobileDevice/Provisioning Profiles"
          echo "$PROFILE_BASE64" | base64 --decode \
            > "$HOME/Library/MobileDevice/Provisioning Profiles/build.mobileprovision"

      - name: Write App Store Connect API key
        env:
          ASC_KEY_BASE64: ${{ secrets.APPLE_ASC_API_KEY_P8 }}
          ASC_KEY_ID: ${{ secrets.APPLE_ASC_API_KEY_ID }}
        run: |
          mkdir -p private_keys
          echo "$ASC_KEY_BASE64" | base64 --decode > "private_keys/AuthKey_${ASC_KEY_ID}.p8"

      - name: Initialize iOS project
        run: npm run tauri ios init

      - name: Build iOS app (App Store export)
        run: npm run ios:build

      - name: Upload to App Store Connect
        env:
          ASC_KEY_ID: ${{ secrets.APPLE_ASC_API_KEY_ID }}
          ASC_ISSUER_ID: ${{ secrets.APPLE_ASC_API_ISSUER_ID }}
        run: |
          IPA=$(find src-tauri/gen/apple/build -name "*.ipa" | head -1)
          echo "Uploading $IPA"
          xcrun altool --upload-app --type ios --file "$IPA" \
            --apiKey "$ASC_KEY_ID" --apiIssuer "$ASC_ISSUER_ID"

name: Deploy GitHub Pages

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
      - master
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read
  pages: write
  id-token: write

concurrency:
  group: pages
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Setup Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20
          cache: npm

      - name: Configure Pages
        uses: actions/configure-pages@v5

      - name: Resolve Pages URLs
        run: |
          OWNER="${{ github.repository_owner }}"
          REPO="${{ github.event.repository.name }}"

          if [ "$REPO" = "$OWNER.github.io" ]; then
            BASE_PATH="/"
            REPO_PREFIX=""
          else
            BASE_PATH="/$REPO/"
            REPO_PREFIX="/$REPO"
          fi

          SITE_URL="https://$OWNER.github.io$REPO_PREFIX"
          OTA_MANIFEST_URL="$SITE_URL/ota/manifest.json"
          OTA_CDN_BASE_URL="$SITE_URL/ota"

          echo "BASE_PATH=$BASE_PATH" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          echo "VITE_OTA_MANIFEST_URL=$OTA_MANIFEST_URL" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          echo "OTA_CDN_BASE_URL=$OTA_CDN_BASE_URL" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm install

      - name: Build web + OTA artifacts
        run: |
          npx tsc
          npx vite build --base "$BASE_PATH"
          npx vite build --config vite.ota.config.ts --base "$BASE_PATH"
          npm run ota:prepare
          touch dist/.nojekyll

      - name: Upload Pages artifact
        uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@v3
        with:
          path: dist

  deploy:
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment:
      name: github-pages
      url: ${{ steps.deployment.outputs.page_url }}
    steps:
      - name: Deploy to GitHub Pages
        id: deployment
        uses: actions/deploy-pages@v4

121	// RecordingService handles audio recording, storage, and transcription.
122	//
123	// save_recording(audio_base64, mime_type, folder_path, file_name_format)
124	//   in:  audio_base64 — base64-encoded audio bytes (may have data URI prefix)
125	//        mime_type — e.g. "audio/webm", "audio/mp4". Defaults to webm
126	//        folder_path — where to create the note, defaults to "Feed"
127	//        file_name_format — how to name the note file
128	//   out: RecordingWriteResult — folder_path, note_path, audio_path (all relative)
129	//   - Decodes the base64 audio and saves to Recordings/ storage folder
130	//   - Audio filename: audio-{uuid}.{ext}
131	//   - Creates a markdown note with front-matter linking to the audio file
132	//   - Front-matter includes: type="audio_recording", recording_audio_path, transcription_status="pending"
133	//   - MIME to extension mapping: mp4/aac→m4a, mpeg/mp3→mp3, wav→wav, ogg→ogg, flac→flac, default→webm
134	//
135	// queue_transcriptions_assembly(api_key)
136	//   in:  api_key — AssemblyAI API key
137	//   out: TranscriptionQueueResult — how many scanned, queued, skipped, in flight
138	//   - Scans all recording notes, skips completed or already-in-flight ones
139	//   - Queues pending/failed recordings for AssemblyAI transcription
140	//   - AssemblyAI flow: upload audio → create transcript → poll every 2s (max 6 min)
141	//   - Speech model: "universal-2"
142	//   - On completion, writes transcript text as the note body
143	//
144	// queue_transcriptions_local(model)
145	//   in:  model — whisper model name, e.g. "large-v3", "tiny", "base", "small", "medium"
146	//   out: TranscriptionQueueResult
147	//   - Same scanning logic as assembly, but uses local faster-whisper via Python subprocess
148	//   - Saves word-level JSON alongside the audio file ({stem}.transcription.json)
149	//   - Requires python3 + faster_whisper installed on the system
150	//
151	// retrigger_transcription(note_path)
152	//   in:  note_path — relative path to the recording note
153	//   out: nothing
154	//   - Resets the note's transcription status to "queued" and re-adds it to the queue
155	//   - Uses local whisper with default model
156	//
157	// list_recordings()
158	//   in:  nothing
159	//   out: RecordingsListResult — queue snapshot + list of all recording notes with status
160	//   - Sorted by updated_ms descending (newest first)
161	//   - Each item includes whether it's currently queued or being processed
162	//
163	// read_recording_audio(path)
164	//   in:  path — relative path to the audio file (must be inside Recordings/ storage)
165	//   out: RecordingAudioPayload — mime_type + audio_base64
166	//   - Only allows reading from the Recordings storage folder (security boundary)
167	//
168	// check_whisper_status()
169	//   in:  nothing
170	//   out: WhisperStatus — whether python3 and faster_whisper are available
171	//   - Runs a lightweight check script to verify the import works
172	//
173	// native_recorder_capabilities()
174	//   in:  nothing
175	//   out: NativeRecorderCapabilities — whether native recording is supported, active, and when it started
176	//   - iOS only: uses AVAudioRecorder for high-quality m4a recording
177	//   - Other platforms: returns supported=false
178	//
179	// start_native_recording()
180	//   in:  nothing
181	//   out: nothing
182	//   - iOS only: configures AVAudioSession, creates AVAudioRecorder, starts recording
183	//   - Fails if already recording
184	//
185	// stop_native_recording()
186	//   in:  nothing
187	//   out: RecordingAudioPayload — mime_type + audio_base64 of the recorded audio
188	//   - iOS only: stops the recorder, reads the file, returns as base64, cleans up
189	//
190	// Key assumptions for any implementation:
191	//   - Audio files are stored in a hidden Recordings/ folder, separate from notes
192	//   - Each recording note links to its audio file via front-matter
193	//   - Transcription is queue-based with a background worker thread
194	//   - Only one transcription runs at a time (sequential processing)
195	//   - Status lifecycle: pending → queued → processing → completed | failed
196	//   - Two transcription backends: local whisper (python subprocess) and AssemblyAI (REST API)

message.content:
This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
   The user (single message at session start) asked: "Please make a react native version of it. Make it a single mono repo, shared modules, shared rust core I guess where possible (where i dont need specifically react native packages) but so for desktop it's Tauri and for mobile React Native." Their explicit priority ranking:
   1. The notetaking interface with folders/feed navigation, frontmatter handling — plain text only at this stage (no rich text)
   2. Convenient git sync compatible with the current Tauri app
   3. Voice recording functionality
   4. Transcription — optional whether it transcribes on the phone ("one option is only transcribe on desktop"); designed so the provider can be swapped later (e.g. iPhone native transcription)
   5. Mobile UI/UX should NOT mimic the current Tauri iOS version — can be rethought entirely, EXCEPT: "when you open app you see 'blank page' onto which you can start typing directly. then the swipe up gesture works the same - the previous note moves up and new blank page gets opened onto which you can start typing again"
   6. "Profiles" = just working folders; a working folder can have a config file (e.g. git repo settings); user can specify the working folder to be "somewhere in files (and not within the app directory itself)"
   - Encryption, pin code, panic mode are secondary ("add it if you have time")
   - Allowed to change/rewrite existing Tauri code; end result: single repo with React Native, Tauri, and shared modules (both Rust and frontend)
   - "if you feel like any refactoring is needed along the way - do it"
   - "before doing it - branch out. then commit along and push along the way" (branch feat/react-native-monorepo already existed and is in use)

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - Monorepo: npm workspaces (apps/*, packages/*) + Cargo workspace at repo root, single Cargo.lock/target and single package-lock.json
   - Hexagonal architecture (domain/application/ports/adapters/commands) — pre-existing in the Tauri backend, exploited for extraction
   - `AppEnv { app_data_dir: PathBuf, documents_dir: Option<PathBuf> }` — the single platform seam replacing `tauri::AppHandle` (which was only used for path resolution)
   - Tauri v2 desktop/mobile cfg aliases replicated via custom build.rs (`cargo:rustc-cfg=desktop|mobile` from CARGO_CFG_TARGET_OS)
   - UniFFI (planned crates/type-ffi) with foreign-implemented trait (`with_foreign`) for pluggable TranscriptionProvider from Swift/Kotlin/JS
   - React Native plan: Expo (prebuild/CNG), uniffi-bindgen-react-native (ubrn) for JSI bindings in packages/mobile-core, typed CoreApi facade so tsc/jest work without native builds, expo-audio for recording, react-native-gesture-handler + reanimated for swipe-up capture stack, react-navigation native-stack, zustand
   - Working-folder config: `<notes_root>/.type/settings.json` (ProfileSettings: git remote/branch/username/password/commit message, mobile auto flags, new transcription_mode) — syncs with the folder via git; device-local secrets in `<app_data>/config.json` (AppConfig: assemblyai_api_key etc.)
   - TranscriptionMode enum: Off | Desktop | AssemblyAi ("assemblyai") | Native, with legacy fallback from mobile_auto_transcription_enabled (true→AssemblyAi, false→Desktop)
   - Transcription queue: process-global worker, TranscriptionMethod enum dispatch (LocalWhisper/AssemblyAi/planned Provider), note status lifecycle pending→queued→processing→completed|failed stored in front matter
   - Desktop already auto-queues pending transcriptions unconditionally (recordings-context.tsx: `isDesktop || syncSettings.mobileAutoTranscriptionEnabled` + useAutoQueueLoop 15s) — so record-on-phone→git-sync→desktop-transcribes works once mobile leaves recordings pending
   - iOS "working folder in Files" v1 approach: app Documents dir visible via UIFileSharingEnabled + LSSupportsOpeningDocumentsInPlace (true external folders later)
   - VM constraints: cannot build iOS/Android here (no Xcode/Android SDK); Tauri Linux deps installed (libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev etc.) so cargo check/test of the whole workspace works locally
   - Sprite environment: checkpoints via `sprite-env checkpoints create --comment "..."`; created v53 (baseline), v55 (M1), v56 (M2)

3. Files and Code Sections:
   - Root `package.json` (created): name "type-monorepo", workspaces ["apps/*", "packages/*"], scripts: desktop:dev/desktop:tauri/desktop:build (→ workspace "type"), mobile:start (→ "@typenotes/mobile"), typecheck/test (`--workspaces --if-present`)
   - Root `Cargo.toml` (created): `[workspace] resolver = "2" members = ["apps/desktop/src-tauri", "crates/type-core"]`
   - `.gitignore`: added `/target/`
   - `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (rewritten): typescript job (node 22, npm install at root, workspace typecheck+test) and rust job (`cargo test --workspace --lib` with apt webkit deps)
   - `.github/workflows/release.yml`: removed rust-cache `workspaces: src-tauri`, `working-directory: apps/desktop` for set-app-version, `projectPath: apps/desktop` for tauri-action, `npm run --workspace type tauri ios init` / `ios:build`, IPA path `apps/desktop/src-tauri/gen/apple/build`
   - `.github/workflows/deploy-pages.yml`: build steps `working-directory: apps/desktop`, artifact path `apps/desktop/dist`
   - `apps/desktop/*` (git mv of src, src-tauri, index.html, public, scripts, components.json, tsconfig*.json, vite*.ts, vitest.config.ts, package.json, .env.example); desktop package.json gained `"typecheck": "tsc --noEmit"`; old root package-lock.json deleted, fresh root lock via npm install; Cargo.lock moved to repo root
   - `crates/type-core/Cargo.toml` (created): lib name type_core; deps: serde{derive}, serde_json, git2 0.20 {vendored-openssl}, base64 0.22, reqwest 0.12 {blocking,json,rustls-tls}, uuid {v7}, time 0.3, argon2 0.5, chacha20poly1305 {std}, zeroize 1.8, zip 0.6 {deflate}, mdns-sd 0.20.0
   - `crates/type-core/build.rs` (created): emits `cargo:rustc-check-cfg=cfg(desktop)/cfg(mobile)` and `cargo:rustc-cfg=desktop|mobile` based on target_os (ios/android → mobile) — required because local_sync.rs uses `#[cfg(desktop)]` 19 times

1	// Shared helpers for the async "job" queues (recording transcription,
2	// handwriting OCR). Both list-item shapes carry the same status fields, so the
3	// preview-invalidation signature is computed the same way for each.
4	
5	type JobSignatureFields = {
6	  note_path: string;
7	  status: string;
8	  updated_ms: number | null;
9	  error: string | null;
10	  is_queued: boolean;
11	  is_processing: boolean;
12	};
13	
14	/**
15	 * Stable signature of a job list, used to decide when note previews need to be
16	 * re-fetched. It is order-independent (sorted), so reordering alone never
17	 * triggers a needless invalidation — only a changed status/timestamp/error does.
18	 */
19	export const jobListSignature = (items: JobSignatureFields[]): string =>
20	  items
21	    .map((item) =>
22	      [
23	        item.note_path,
24	        item.status,
25	        item.updated_ms ?? "",
26	        item.error ?? "",
27	        item.is_queued ? "1" : "0",
28	        item.is_processing ? "1" : "0",
29	      ].join("|")
30	    )
31	    .sort()
32	    .join("||");

/**
 * Normalize an unknown thrown value into a human-readable message.
 *
 * `catch` clauses receive `unknown`, so the same `error instanceof Error`
 * narrowing was previously inlined dozens of times across features. Use this
 * helper instead so error formatting stays consistent in one place.
 *
 * Note: domain-specific formatters (e.g. the recorder's DOMException handling
 * in `use-audio-recorder`) intentionally do their own thing — this is only the
 * generic fallback.
 */
export const getErrorMessage = (error: unknown): string =>
  error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error);

content.subject: M1: Restructure repo into monorepo (apps/desktop + npm/cargo workspaces + CI)
content.description: Move desktop app (src/, src-tauri/, vite configs, package.json…) to apps/desktop; root npm workspaces + root Cargo workspace; update CI workflows and doc pointers; verify tsc/vitest/vite build (and cargo if system libs available). Commit + push.

content.subject: M2: Extract framework-free Rust core crate (crates/type-core)
content.description: Move domain/application/ports + pure adapters (notes, profiles, security, recordings queue+assembly, whisper_env desktop-gated, handwriting, import, git, local_sync desktop-gated) into crates/type-core. Replace tauri::AppHandle with AppEnv { app_data_dir, documents_dir }. Tauri crate keeps commands + platform/ios adapters and depends on core. cargo test core standalone.

content.subject: M3: Working-folder config + transcription mode in core
content.description: Per-working-folder config file inside notes_root (git repo settings etc.), profiles = registry of working folders. Transcription policy enum (off / desktop-only / cloud AssemblyAI / pluggable native provider port) so phones can defer transcription to desktop; desktop auto-queues pending recordings after sync.

content.subject: M4: UniFFI bindings crate (crates/type-ffi)
content.description: uniffi crate exposing init(appDataDir), working folders/profiles, notes (tree/read/write/create/move/delete/rename/previews), git sync (status/connect/pull/push/ssh keys), recordings save + transcription queue, foreign-trait TranscriptionProvider hook. Host cargo tests.

content.subject: M5: Shared TS package (packages/shared)
content.description: Extract platform-free TS from src/shared (frontmatter, note preview/format, annotation-metadata, jobs, domain types) into packages/shared; desktop consumes it; RN app consumes it. tsc + vitest green.

content.subject: M6: React Native app (apps/mobile) + native core module
content.description: Expo (prebuild) RN app: blank-page capture screen with swipe-up-to-new-note stack, feed/folders navigation, plain-text editor, git sync screen, voice recording (expo-audio) → core saveRecording, settings (working folders, transcription mode). packages/mobile-core RN library wrapping type-ffi via uniffi-bindgen-react-native (generated bindings checked in; iOS/Android build docs). Core access behind a typed facade so jest/tsc pass without native builds.

content.subject: M7: Docs + CI final pass
content.description: Update AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md/README for monorepo layout, new crates/packages, mobile build steps (mac: rustup targets, ubrn codegen, pod install). CI: workspace test matrix incl. core crate + ffi + mobile tsc/jest.

content.subject: M8 (stretch): Security/PIN surfaces on mobile
content.description: Expose security state/unlock/enable/panic via FFI + minimal PIN lock screen in RN app. Only if time remains after M1–M7.

git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
Extract platform-free TS into packages/shared (@typenotes/shared)

New npm workspace package shared by the desktop app and the upcoming
React Native app: domain types, frontmatter parsing, note-preview
formatting (format), annotation-metadata + lens-backmatter stripping,
job-queue signatures, error normalization, pure folder-tree walkers
(notes), and system-folder constants (Feed / Archieve).

The package exports TS source directly ("./*": "./src/*.ts" — the
internal-package pattern), so Vite, tsc, and Metro consume it without a
build step. Its tsconfig has no DOM lib, which keeps browser APIs from
creeping into shared code. Browser-only helpers (yieldToUi, base64,
dom/storage/selection, UI constants) stay in apps/desktop/src/shared.

Desktop imports moved from @/shared/... to @typenotes/shared/<module>.
Typecheck and vitest are green in both workspaces (54 + 18 tests).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF

# @typenotes/mobile-core

The React Native app's bridge to the shared Rust core (`crates/type-ffi`,
UniFFI bindings over `crates/type-core`).

## How it fits together

```
apps/mobile  ──imports──▶  core-api.ts   (typed facade, JSON marshalling)
                              │
                              ▼
                          raw-core.ts    (RawCore interface + setRawCore seam)
                              ▲
              ┌───────────────┴────────────────┐
   src/generated/* (ubrn codegen,       mock-core.ts (in-memory,
   real Rust core — Mac build only)     demo mode / tests / Expo Go)
```

- **`src/core-api.ts`** — what the app imports. Typed functions
  (`getTree(): Promise<FolderNode>`, `gitPush(args)`, …) that serialize to the
  same serde JSON the desktop Tauri commands use (types from
  `@typenotes/shared/types`).
- **`src/raw-core.ts`** — the `RawCore` interface mirroring the UniFFI exports
  one-to-one, plus `setRawCore()`. The app wires an implementation at startup.
- **`src/mock-core.ts`** — in-memory `RawCore` used by tests and as demo mode
  when the native module isn't linked. Nothing persists.

This layout keeps `tsc`, `vitest`, and Expo Go working with **no native
builds** — the generated turbo module is only required for a real device build.

## Generating the native module (Mac only)

Prerequisites: Xcode (+ `rustup target add aarch64-apple-ios aarch64-apple-ios-sim`),
and/or Android Studio + NDK (+ `rustup target add aarch64-linux-android armv7-linux-androideabi`).

```sh
npm install -D uniffi-bindgen-react-native@0.31.0-3   # in this package
npx ubrn checkout --config ubrn.config.yaml            # no-op, crate is local
npx ubrn build ios     --config ubrn.config.yaml --and-generate
npx ubrn build android --config ubrn.config.yaml --and-generate
```

This produces `src/generated/` (TS bindings), `cpp/generated/` (JSI glue), and
the `ios/` / `android/` library projects. Then wire the generated module in
the app instead of the mock (`apps/mobile/src/core/boot.ts`):

```ts
import { setRawCore } from "@typenotes/mobile-core/raw-core";
import * as generated from "@typenotes/mobile-core/generated";
setRawCore(generated);
```

The generated function names match `RawCore` (uniffi camelCases the Rust
snake_case exports). If a signature drifts after changing `crates/type-ffi`,
update `raw-core.ts` and `core-api.ts` to match — the desktop commands and
`crates/type-ffi/src/tests.rs` are the source of truth for the JSON shapes.

Generated output is gitignored; regenerate after every `crates/type-ffi`
change. Finally run `npx pod-install` in `apps/mobile/ios` after an Expo
prebuild (see `apps/mobile/README.md`).

## Transcription providers

`queueProviderTranscriptions(provider)` passes a host-side implementation of
the FFI foreign trait to the Rust queue worker — this is how native on-device
speech recognition plugs in without touching core:

```ts
await queueProviderTranscriptions({
  id: () => "apple-speech",
  transcribe: (audioPath) => recognizeWithSFSpeech(audioPath),
});
```

Use it when the active working folder's `transcription_mode` is `"native"`.
`"assemblyai"` uses `queueRecordingTranscriptions()` (cloud); `"desktop"`
leaves recordings `pending` so a synced desktop transcribes them with local
Whisper; `"off"` never queues automatically.

input.content:
# Type — mobile (React Native / Expo)

The React Native version of Type. Same Rust core as the desktop app
(`crates/type-core` via `crates/type-ffi`), same on-disk format, same git
sync — a folder of markdown files with front matter, `Feed`/`Archieve`
system folders, and per-folder `.type/settings.json`.

## The one interaction that matters

The app opens on a **blank page** — start typing immediately. **Swipe up**
and the page files itself into Feed while a fresh blank page slides in
underneath. Everything else (feed, folders, sync, recording, settings) is
secondary chrome reachable from the corner buttons.

## Running it

### Demo mode (no native build — works anywhere, including Expo Go)

```sh
npm install            # at the repo root (npm workspaces)
npm run start -w @typenotes/mobile
```

Without the generated native module the app boots against an in-memory mock
core (`@typenotes/mobile-core/mock-core`): fully interactive, nothing
persisted, banner at the bottom. UI work and the vitest suites never need a
native build.

### Real build (Mac)

1. Generate the native core module — see `packages/mobile-core/README.md`
   (ubrn codegen + iOS/Android Rust builds).
2. Wire it in `src/core/boot.ts` (uncomment the generated-module import).
3. Prebuild and run:

```sh
npm run prebuild -w @typenotes/mobile    # expo prebuild → ios/ + android/
npm run ios -w @typenotes/mobile         # or: npm run android -w @typenotes/mobile
```

The iOS app's Documents directory is user-visible in the Files app
(`UIFileSharingEnabled` + `LSSupportsOpeningDocumentsInPlace`), so working
folders created under it can be browsed, backed up, and pointed at from
other apps. True security-scoped external folders (iCloud Drive etc.) are a
later step.

## Layout

```
src/
  App.tsx                 boot + navigation container + demo banner
  navigation.ts           typed native-stack route table
  theme.ts                light/dark palette
  core/boot.ts            wires RawCore (generated native module or mock) + initCore
  lib/capture.ts          capture-page note lifecycle (pure, tested)
  lib/feed.ts             tree+previews → list rows (pure, tested)
  state/                  zustand stores: notes, settings (working folders), sync
  screens/                capture, feed, folder, editor, record, sync, settings
  ui/controls.tsx         small shared primitives for the utility screens
```

State flows one way: screens → `@typenotes/mobile-core/core-api` (typed
facade over the FFI) → Rust core. Stores cache the tree/previews/status and
re-fetch after mutations. Preview parsing, date labels, sync-error hints,
and frontmatter helpers come from `@typenotes/shared` — the same code the
desktop app uses.

## Transcription

Recordings are saved through the core (note + audio file + front matter,
`transcription_status: pending`), then queued according to the working
folder's `transcription_mode` (`.type/settings.json`, synced with the
notes): `assemblyai` queues cloud transcription from the phone, `desktop`
leaves recordings pending for a synced desktop's local Whisper, `native` is
the hook for an on-device recognizer via `queueProviderTranscriptions`
(provider registration not wired yet), `off` does nothing.

content.content: Updated task #7 activeForm, status

1	# Type
2	
3	A **local-first markdown notes app**. Your notes are plain `.md` files in a folder on
4	your own disk — no account, no lock-in, readable and editable by any other tool. Optional
5	Git sync keeps them in step across devices, including a one-button local-network server so
6	a phone can sync over Wi-Fi or a hotspot with **no external host**.
7	
8	Built with **Tauri v2** (Rust backend) and **React 19 / TypeScript** (frontend). Runs on
9	macOS, Windows, Linux, and iOS.
10	
11	## Highlights
12	
13	- **Plain-file storage** — notes are `.md` files in a folder tree you can point anywhere; order persists per folder.
14	- **Rich markdown editor** (Tiptap) with debounced autosave and content-based auto-naming.
15	- **Git sync** over `https://`, `ssh://`, or `git://` — push/pull across devices via libgit2 (no shell `git` needed).
16	- **One-button local sync** — host a `git daemon` on the desktop; the phone finds it by mDNS or QR code, no typing.
17	- **SSH key auth** — generate an Ed25519 keypair in-app for passwordless SSH.
18	- **Never-blocked merges** — conflicts keep your version and drop the remote copy beside it as `.conflict.md`.
19	- **Audio recording + transcription** — zero-install local Whisper on desktop, AssemblyAI on iOS.
20	- **Handwriting OCR** — import an image, get text back (OpenAI / Hugging Face).
21	- **Processing queues** — voice transcription and handwriting OCR run as separate queues with shared status plumbing.
22	- **Multi-profile** — independent notes roots and sync settings.
23	- **Extension surfaces** — multi-note lens and note encryption/lock/panic are kept behind a typed frontend registry.
24	- **Desktop & mobile UIs** — resizable three-pane on desktop; native-feeling stack/split navigation on phone/tablet.
25	
26	## Tech stack & architecture
27	
28	- **Frontend** — React 19, TypeScript, Vite, Zustand, Tiptap, DnD Kit, Tailwind +
29	  shadcn/ui. Feature-sliced domains feed separate desktop and mobile composition shells.
30	  Feature-sliced under `src/`: `app/` (composition root), `shared/` (domain-agnostic
31	  building blocks), `features/<domain>/`, optional `features/extensions/`, shared
32	  queue plumbing under `features/processing/`, plus thin `desktop/` and `mobile/` shells.
33	  Context providers are intentionally slim: state/action/workflow hooks carry the notes tree,
34	  profile, git sync, processing, command palette, and desktop editor/navigation workflows.
35	  Optional surfaces such as multi-note lens are extension-gated and lazy-loaded where possible.
36	- **Backend** — Tauri v2 (Rust) in a pragmatic **domain / application / ports / adapters / commands**

# Type

A **local-first markdown notes app**. Your notes are plain `.md` files in a folder on
your own disk — no account, no lock-in, readable and editable by any other tool. Optional
Git sync keeps them in step across devices, including a one-button local-network server so
a phone can sync over Wi-Fi or a hotspot with **no external host**.

Built with **Tauri v2** (Rust backend) and **React 19 / TypeScript** (frontend). Runs on
macOS, Windows, Linux, and iOS.

## Highlights

- **Plain-file storage** — notes are `.md` files in a folder tree you can point anywhere; order persists per folder.
- **Rich markdown editor** (Tiptap) with debounced autosave and content-based auto-naming.
- **Git sync** over `https://`, `ssh://`, or `git://` — push/pull across devices via libgit2 (no shell `git` needed).
- **One-button local sync** — host a `git daemon` on the desktop; the phone finds it by mDNS or QR code, no typing.
- **SSH key auth** — generate an Ed25519 keypair in-app for passwordless SSH.
- **Never-blocked merges** — conflicts keep your version and drop the remote copy beside it as `.conflict.md`.
- **Audio recording + transcription** — zero-install local Whisper on desktop, AssemblyAI on iOS.
- **Handwriting OCR** — import an image, get text back (OpenAI / Hugging Face).
- **Processing queues** — voice transcription and handwriting OCR run as separate queues with shared status plumbing.
- **Multi-profile** — independent notes roots and sync settings.
- **Extension surfaces** — multi-note lens and note encryption/lock/panic are kept behind a typed frontend registry.
- **Desktop & mobile UIs** — resizable three-pane on desktop; native-feeling stack/split navigation on phone/tablet.

## Tech stack & architecture

- **Frontend** — React 19, TypeScript, Vite, Zustand, Tiptap, DnD Kit, Tailwind +
  shadcn/ui. Feature-sliced domains feed separate desktop and mobile composition shells.
  Feature-sliced under `src/`: `app/` (composition root), `shared/` (domain-agnostic
  building blocks), `features/<domain>/`, optional `features/extensions/`, shared
  queue plumbing under `features/processing/`, plus thin `desktop/` and `mobile/` shells.
  Context providers are intentionally slim: state/action/workflow hooks carry the notes tree,
  profile, git sync, processing, command palette, and desktop editor/navigation workflows.
  Optional surfaces such as multi-note lens are extension-gated and lazy-loaded where possible.
- **Backend** — Tauri v2 (Rust) in a pragmatic **domain / application / ports / adapters / commands**
  layout, so use cases can move to another shell (e.g. UniFFI for React Native) without a rewrite.

**[src-tauri/README.md](src-tauri/README.md)**.

If you want a gentler architecture introduction in Russian, read
**[docs/architecture](docs/architecture/README.md)**.

## Architecture rationale

### Why these layers?

| Layer | Role | Depends on |
|-------|------|------------|
| **domain** | Framework-free DTOs and domain state. | Nothing app-specific. |
| **application** | Use-case orchestration and policy. | `ports` + `domain`. |
| **ports** | Traits for outbound dependencies and gateway contracts. | `domain` types. |
| **adapters** | Concrete filesystem, git2, crypto, HTTP, native APIs. | `ports`, external crates, Tauri where needed. |
| **commands** | IPC transport, security gate, blocking-thread dispatch. | `application`, concrete adapters, Tauri. |

The key rule: **commands do not own business workflows**. They unlock-gate the
request, construct the relevant application service, and dispatch blocking work
when needed. Application services depend on traits, while adapters own Tauri
handles, filesystem paths, git2, HTTP, crypto, native APIs, and worker queues.

The notes domain is the strictest implementation: note DTOs live in `domain/`,
note use cases live in `application/notes.rs`, and filesystem/frontmatter/git
history/time/id/encryption dependencies are accessed through ports. Other
domains now follow the same command -> application -> port -> adapter direction
through gateway traits while their deeper persistence logic remains in adapters.

### Why split commands by domain?

Previously `commands.rs` was a single 1354-line file containing every Tauri
command handler. Splitting into domain modules:

1. **Readability** — each file covers one concern and fits on screen.
2. **Migration surface** — when swapping Tauri for UniFFI, you can migrate one
   domain at a time (e.g. swap `commands/notes.rs` while keeping the rest on
   Tauri).
3. **Parallel work** — contributors can work on different domains without merge
   conflicts in a single monolithic file.

### How commands reference use cases

Each command submodule imports its application service and concrete Tauri
adapter explicitly. The `generate_handler![]` macro in `commands/mod.rs` uses
qualified paths (`security::get_security_state`, `notes::read_note`, etc.) to
avoid ambiguity with identically-named adapter modules.

### Future: UniFFI migration path

The planned migration to React Native with `uniffi-bindgen-react-native`:

1. Keep `domain/`, `application/`, `ports/`, and most `adapters/` as-is.
2. Replace `commands/` with UniFFI `#[uniffi::export]` functions that construct
   the same application services.
3. The frontend moves from Tauri's IPC to UniFFI-generated TypeScript bindings.

Because the command layer is intentionally thin, this swap is mechanical rather
than architectural.

# src-tauri — the desktop (Tauri) shell

This crate is the **Tauri v2 shell** around the shared Rust core. Almost all
business logic — the **domain / application / ports / adapters** layers — lives
in [`crates/type-core`](../../../crates/type-core), which is framework-free and
also powers the mobile FFI ([`crates/type-ffi`](../../../crates/type-ffi),
UniFFI bindings consumed by the React Native app). What remains here is the
IPC transport and the platform pieces only a Tauri process can provide.

## Directory layout

```
src/
├── lib.rs              Crate root: app_env() (tauri::AppHandle → type_core::AppEnv),
│                       macOS window-alpha helpers, and the public run() entry point.
├── main.rs             Binary entry point (calls lib::run).
│
├── adapters/
│   ├── platform.rs     Native theme + file-export sheet (Tauri/objc APIs).
│   ├── recordings.rs   TauriRecordingsAdapter: wraps the core RecordingsAdapter
│   │                   and overrides the three native-capture methods on iOS.
│   └── ios.rs          (iOS only) AVAudioRecorder/AVAudioSession recording and
│                       WKWebView termination recovery via ObjC interop.
│
├── application/platform.rs   Platform use-case facade (the one domain that
├── ports/platform.rs         stays shell-side: theme + export sheet).
│
└── commands/           Thin #[tauri::command] wrappers, one file per domain.
    ├── mod.rs          App bootstrap (Tauri Builder, plugins, generate_handler!)
    │                   and the shared run_blocking_command helper.
    ├── security.rs     lock, unlock, enable, preferences, state.
    ├── platform.rs     native theme, file export sheet.
    ├── profiles.rs     profile CRUD, backup zip, Documents export, app config.
    ├── notes.rs        tree, read/create/write, meta, previews, move/delete/
    │                   rename, order, timestamps, markers.
    ├── recordings.rs   native recorder, save, transcription queues, list.
    ├── handwriting.rs  save attachment, OCR queue, list jobs.
    ├── import.rs       Apple Notes scan / start / status.
    ├── git_sync.rs     SSH keys, status, history, connect, pull, push.
    └── local_sync.rs   local git-daemon server, mDNS discovery.
```

## How a command flows

```
frontend invoke("read_note")
  → commands/notes.rs        (lock gate, arg structs — from type_core)
  → type_core::application   (use-case service, depends on port traits)
  → type_core::adapters      (filesystem, git2, crypto, HTTP, workers)
```

Commands do not own business workflows. Each command file builds the relevant
`type_core` application service with the concrete core adapter, passing
`crate::app_env(&app)?` — the `AppEnv { app_data_dir, documents_dir }` seam
that replaced direct `tauri::AppHandle` usage when the core was extracted.
`ensure_security_unlocked_for_app` gates content commands while locked.

The `generate_handler![]` macro in `commands/mod.rs` uses qualified paths
(`notes::read_note`, `git_sync::git_pull`, …) to disambiguate command modules.

## What stays in the shell, and why

| Piece | Reason |
|-------|--------|
| `commands/` | Tauri IPC is the transport; the FFI crate is the other transport over the same services. |
| `platform` domain | Native theming and the file-export sheet need the Tauri window / ObjC. |
| iOS native capture | AVAudioRecorder + WKWebView recovery need the app's ObjC runtime. |
| `app_env()` | Path resolution (`app_data_dir`, `documents_dir`) is the only thing the core needs from Tauri. |

The "future UniFFI migration path" this README used to describe has happened:
`crates/type-ffi` exports the same use cases with `#[uniffi::export]` for the
React Native app. When adding a feature, put the logic in `type-core`, then
expose it twice — a thin command here, a thin export there.

# src-tauri — Rust Backend

This is the Rust backend for the app, built on Tauri v2. The code is organised
using a pragmatic **clean / hexagonal architecture** so that core use cases can
move to a different shell later (e.g. UniFFI bindings for a React Native mobile
app) without rewriting domain logic.

## Directory layout

```
src/
├── lib.rs              Crate root — module declarations, shared constants,
│                       utility functions, and the public run() entry point.
├── main.rs             Binary entry point (calls lib::run).
│
├── domain/             Framework-free core DTOs and domain state.
│   └── notes.rs        Note tree, metadata, frontmatter, create/order args.
│
├── application/        Use-case services. Owns workflows and depends on ports,
│                       never on Tauri command handlers.
│   ├── notes.rs        Real note CRUD/tree/order workflows.
│   ├── profiles.rs     Profile use-case facade.
│   ├── security.rs     Lock/encryption use-case facade.
│   ├── recordings.rs   Recording/native capture/transcription facade.
│   ├── handwriting.rs  Attachment/OCR facade.
│   ├── import.rs       Import scan/start/status facade.
│   ├── git_sync.rs     Git sync facade.
│   ├── local_sync.rs   Local sync server facade.
│   └── platform.rs     Native platform facade.
│
├── ports/              Port interfaces and gateway traits.
│   ├── mod.rs          Module index.
│   ├── notes.rs        Note CRUD, tree, ordering.
│   ├── profiles.rs     Multi-profile management.
│   ├── security.rs     Encryption, locking, key derivation.
│   ├── recordings.rs   Audio recording & transcription.
│   ├── handwriting.rs  Handwriting OCR pipeline.
│   ├── git_sync.rs     Git sync (SSH/HTTPS, merge, history).
│   └── platform.rs     Platform-specific capabilities (theme, export).
│
├── adapters/           Adapter implementations (Rust/Tauri/filesystem-specific).
│   ├── mod.rs          Module index + crate-level re-exports.
│   ├── notes/          Filesystem-backed note storage + document codec.
│   ├── profiles.rs     JSON-file profile state management.
│   ├── security.rs     XChaCha20-Poly1305 encryption, Argon2 KDF.
│   ├── recordings.rs   Audio file handling, Whisper/AssemblyAI transcription.
│   ├── handwriting.rs  Image attachment handling, LLM-based OCR.
│   ├── git.rs          git2-based sync (fetch, merge, push, history).
│   └── ios.rs          iOS native integration (AVFoundation, ObjC interop).
│
└── commands/           Tauri command layer (thin wrappers, one file per domain).
    ├── mod.rs          App bootstrap (Tauri Builder, plugins, generate_handler!)
    │                   and the shared run_blocking_command helper.
    ├── security.rs     5 commands  — lock, unlock, enable, preferences, state.
    ├── platform.rs     2 commands  — native theme, file export sheet.
    ├── profiles.rs     8 commands  — CRUD, backup, export.
    ├── notes.rs        10 commands — tree, read, create, write, move, delete, rename, order.
    ├── recordings.rs   10 commands — native recorder, save, transcription queue, list.
    ├── handwriting.rs  3 commands  — save attachment, OCR queue, list jobs.
    └── git_sync.rs     8 commands  — SSH keys, status, history, connect, pull, push.
```

## Architecture rationale

### Why these layers?

| Layer | Role | Depends on |
|-------|------|------------|
| **domain** | Framework-free DTOs and domain state. | Nothing app-specific. |
| **application** | Use-case orchestration and policy. | `ports` + `domain`. |
| **ports** | Traits for outbound dependencies and gateway contracts. | `domain` types. |
| **adapters** | Concrete filesystem, git2, crypto, HTTP, native APIs. | `ports`, external crates, Tauri where needed. |
| **commands** | IPC transport, security gate, blocking-thread dispatch. | `application`, concrete adapters, Tauri. |

The key rule: **commands do not own business workflows**. They unlock-gate the
request, construct the relevant application service, and dispatch blocking work
when needed. Application services depend on traits, while adapters own Tauri
handles, filesystem paths, git2, HTTP, crypto, native APIs, and worker queues.

The notes domain is the strictest implementation: note DTOs live in `domain/`,
note use cases live in `application/notes.rs`, and filesystem/frontmatter/git
history/time/id/encryption dependencies are accessed through ports. Other
domains now follow the same command -> application -> port -> adapter direction
through gateway traits while their deeper persistence logic remains in adapters.

### Why split commands by domain?

Previously `commands.rs` was a single 1354-line file containing every Tauri
command handler. Splitting into domain modules:

1. **Readability** — each file covers one concern and fits on screen.
2. **Migration surface** — when swapping Tauri for UniFFI, you can migrate one
   domain at a time (e.g. swap `commands/notes.rs` while keeping the rest on
   Tauri).
3. **Parallel work** — contributors can work on different domains without merge
   conflicts in a single monolithic file.

### How commands reference use cases

Each command submodule imports its application service and concrete Tauri
adapter explicitly. The `generate_handler![]` macro in `commands/mod.rs` uses
qualified paths (`security::get_security_state`, `notes::read_note`, etc.) to
avoid ambiguity with identically-named adapter modules.

### Future: UniFFI migration path

The planned migration to React Native with `uniffi-bindgen-react-native`:

1. Keep `domain/`, `application/`, `ports/`, and most `adapters/` as-is.
2. Replace `commands/` with UniFFI `#[uniffi::export]` functions that construct
   the same application services.
3. The frontend moves from Tauri's IPC to UniFFI-generated TypeScript bindings.

Because the command layer is intentionally thin, this swap is mechanical rather
than architectural.

# AGENTS.md

This document is for AI agents and developers who need to understand and modify this codebase.

## What this app is

A local-first markdown notes app. Notes are stored as `.md` files in a local folder tree ("working folders"), with optional Git sync across devices — including a one-button local-network server (`git daemon`) for syncing to a phone with no external host. Audio recording is supported, with per-folder transcription routing (local Whisper on desktop — self-provisioning, no manual install; AssemblyAI cloud; a pluggable native provider; or "leave pending for the desktop to transcribe after sync"). Handwriting OCR and voice transcription use independent queues with shared frontend queue plumbing. At-rest note-body encryption, the lock screen, panic-password local wipe, and the multi-note lens are optional frontend extension surfaces.
