# AGENTS.md

This document is for AI agents and developers who need to understand and modify this codebase.

## What this app is

A local-first markdown notes app. Notes are stored as `.md` files in a local folder tree ("working folders"), with optional Git sync across devices — including a one-button local-network server (`git daemon`) for syncing to a phone with no external host. Audio recording is supported, with per-folder transcription routing (local Whisper on desktop — self-provisioning, no manual install; AssemblyAI cloud; a pluggable native provider; or "leave pending for the desktop to transcribe after sync"). Handwriting OCR and voice transcription use independent queues with shared frontend queue plumbing. At-rest note-body encryption, the lock screen, panic-password local wipe, and the multi-note lens are optional frontend extension surfaces.

There are **two apps over one Rust core**: the desktop app is Tauri v2 + React (also runs the legacy Tauri-iOS build), and the mobile app is React Native (Expo), talking to the same core through UniFFI bindings.

## Monorepo layout

npm workspaces (`apps/*`, `packages/*`) + one Cargo workspace at the repo root
(single `Cargo.lock` and `target/`).

```
apps/desktop/          The Tauri app: React frontend (src/) + Tauri shell (src-tauri/)
apps/mobile/           The React Native app (Expo). See apps/mobile/README.md
crates/type-core/      Framework-free Rust core: domain/application/ports/adapters
crates/type-ffi/       UniFFI bindings over type-core for non-Tauri shells
packages/shared/       @typenotes/shared — platform-free TS (domain types,
                       frontmatter, note previews, sync hints) used by both apps
packages/mobile-core/  @typenotes/mobile-core — typed TS bridge to type-ffi
                       (RawCore seam + in-memory mock; native module generated
                       on a Mac with uniffi-bindgen-react-native)
```

- **Desktop frontend**: React 19, TypeScript, Vite, Tiptap (editor), DnD Kit (drag-and-drop), Tailwind + Shadcn/ui

The Rust core uses a pragmatic **domain / application / ports / adapters**
layout, framework-free so both shells (Tauri commands, UniFFI exports) drive
the same use cases. The shell-facing seam is `AppEnv { app_data_dir,
documents_dir }` — the only thing a shell must provide.

## Mobile app (apps/mobile) + FFI bridge

The React Native app (Expo) reuses the Rust core through
`crates/type-ffi` → `packages/mobile-core` → screens/stores:

- **`crates/type-ffi`** — `#[uniffi::export(async_runtime = "tokio")]`
  functions per domain, JSON-string args/results matching the Tauri IPC
  shapes, so one set of TS wire types (`@typenotes/shared/types`) fits both
  shells. `init_core(app_data_dir, documents_dir)` must run first.
  `TranscriptionProvider` is a foreign trait (`with_foreign`): Swift/Kotlin/JS
  implementations run inside the core's queue worker.
- **`packages/mobile-core`** — `raw-core.ts` (the `RawCore` interface + a
  `setRawCore()` seam), `core-api.ts` (typed facade the app imports), and
  `mock-core.ts` (in-memory RawCore for vitest and "demo mode"). The real
  turbo module is generated on a Mac with `uniffi-bindgen-react-native`
  (ubrn 0.31.x = uniffi 0.31); output dirs are gitignored. Regenerate after
  any `type-ffi` change and keep `raw-core.ts` in sync.
- **`apps/mobile`** — the signature interaction: the app opens on a blank
  page (type immediately); swipe up files the page into Feed and a fresh
  blank page appears. `src/lib/capture.ts` (pure, tested) owns that note
  lifecycle with the same rules as the desktop editor (lazy create,
  debounced writes, flush on leave, empty-note cleanup). Screens: feed,
  folder browser, plain-text editor, record (expo-audio → `save_audio_recording`
  → queue per `transcription_mode`), sync (status/connect/pull/push/SSH
  key/history), settings (working folders, notes-root move, transcription
  mode, AssemblyAI key). Zustand stores in `src/state/`. Without the native
  module the app boots the mock core in demo mode (bottom banner) — that is
  what CI and Expo Go exercise.

# Type

A **local-first markdown notes app**. Your notes are plain `.md` files in a folder on
your own disk — no account, no lock-in, readable and editable by any other tool. Optional
Git sync keeps them in step across devices, including a one-button local-network server so
a phone can sync over Wi-Fi or a hotspot with **no external host**.

Built with **Tauri v2** (Rust backend) and **React 19 / TypeScript** (frontend). Runs on
macOS, Windows, Linux, and iOS.

# Type

A **local-first markdown notes app**. Your notes are plain `.md` files in a folder on
your own disk — no account, no lock-in, readable and editable by any other tool. Optional
Git sync keeps them in step across devices, including a one-button local-network server so
a phone can sync over Wi-Fi or a hotspot with **no external host**.

Two apps share **one Rust core**:

- **Desktop** — Tauri v2 + React 19/TypeScript (macOS, Windows, Linux; also the legacy Tauri-iOS build)
- **Mobile** — React Native (Expo), talking to the same core through UniFFI. Opens on a
  blank page you can type on immediately; swipe up files it away and gives you a fresh page.

npm workspaces + one Cargo workspace:

crates/type-core/      Framework-free Rust core (notes, git sync, recordings,
                       transcription queues, security, working folders)
crates/type-ffi/       UniFFI bindings over type-core for the mobile app
packages/shared/       @typenotes/shared — platform-free TS used by both apps
packages/mobile-core/  @typenotes/mobile-core — typed TS bridge to type-ffi
```

content.text:
All milestones are done. The branch `feat/react-native-monorepo` now contains the complete monorepo, pushed through `524195a` (checkpoints v70–v73 along the way).

## What you have now

```
apps/desktop/          Tauri app, unchanged behavior — now a thin shell over the core
apps/mobile/           React Native app (Expo SDK 57, RN 0.86)
crates/type-core/      Framework-free Rust core (all business logic)
crates/type-ffi/       UniFFI bindings over the core for React Native
packages/shared/       Platform-free TS both apps use (types, frontmatter, previews)
packages/mobile-core/  Typed TS bridge: RawCore seam + core-api + in-memory mock
```

Against your priority list:
1. **Notetaking** — blank-page capture on open, plain-text only; feed and folder navigation; frontmatter handled by the same Rust core the desktop uses, so files are byte-compatible.
2. **Git sync** — the mobile sync screen drives the identical libgit2 core: status, connect, pull/push, app-managed SSH key, history. Same `.type/settings.json`, same `.conflict.md` merge rule.
3. **Voice recording** — expo-audio capture → `save_audio_recording` (note + audio + `pending` front matter).
4. **Transcription** — per-folder `transcription_mode` in `.type/settings.json` (syncs with notes): `assemblyai` on-phone, `desktop` (record on phone, desktop transcribes after sync — this works today since desktop auto-queues pending recordings), `native` (pluggable `TranscriptionProvider` FFI trait for e.g. iPhone speech recognition), `off`.
5. **UX rethought** — nothing carried over except the swipe-up: page files itself into Feed, fresh blank page appears underneath.
6. **Working folders** — profiles are just folders with a config file; you can move a folder's root to an absolute path from mobile settings, and the app's Documents dir is visible in the Files app.
7. **Bonus (M8)** — mobile lock screen: unlock/panic/auto-lock-on-background over the existing security core.

## What needs a Mac (documented, can't run here)

The Rust native module for the phone: `ubrn` codegen + iOS/Android cross-builds, then one wiring line in `apps/mobile/src/core/boot.ts`. Steps are in `packages/mobile-core/README.md` and `apps/mobile/README.md`. Until then the app boots in **demo mode** (in-memory mock core, banner shown) — it runs in Expo Go right now via `npm run mobile:start`.

## Caveats worth knowing

- **Verification**: all four TS workspaces typecheck + test green locally (54 + 18 + 10 tests, plus 15 Rust tests at M3). Heavy cargo checks since M4 are deferred to CI per your ask — but **CI only triggers on PRs**, so opening a (draft) PR is the quickest way to get the full matrix. `TODO.md` tracks every deferred check.
- **Pre-existing issue I'd flag**: `git_password` is persisted in plaintext inside the synced notes root (`.type/settings.json`) — it predates this branch but is more visible now that the file syncs. Worth moving to device-local config at some point.
- This VM segfaults vitest's parallel pool — locally run `vitest run --no-file-parallelism`; CI is unaffected.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Local release fallback — same outcome as the GitHub Actions Release workflow,
# but built on your own Mac. Use this once you exhaust the free macOS CI minutes,
# or any time you'd rather build locally.
#
# Usage:
#   scripts/release-local.sh <version> <desktop|ios|both>
#
# Examples:
#   scripts/release-local.sh 1.2.3 desktop
#   scripts/release-local.sh 1.2.4 both
#
# Prerequisites:
#   - Run on macOS.
#   - `gh auth login` done (used to create the GitHub Release for desktop).
#   - Desktop: TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY + TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD set
#     (see docs/RELEASING.md). The key is the one from `tauri signer generate`.
#   - iOS: Apple signing set up locally (same as your existing `npm run ios:build`).
set -euo pipefail

VERSION="${1:-}"
PLATFORMS="${2:-both}"
REPO="oogxdd/type_new"   # owner/name used in the updater download URLs

if [ -z "$VERSION" ]; then
  echo "usage: $0 <version> <desktop|ios|both>" >&2
  exit 1
fi

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
cd "$ROOT"

DO_DESKTOP=false
DO_IOS=false
case "$PLATFORMS" in
  both)    DO_DESKTOP=true; DO_IOS=true ;;
  desktop) DO_DESKTOP=true ;;
  ios)     DO_IOS=true ;;
  *) echo "platform must be desktop | ios | both" >&2; exit 1 ;;
esac

TAG="v$VERSION"
echo "==> Releasing $TAG (desktop=$DO_DESKTOP ios=$DO_IOS)"

bash scripts/set-app-version.sh "$VERSION"

if [ "$DO_DESKTOP" = true ]; then
  : "${TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY:?set TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY (the updater private key)}"
  : "${TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD:?set TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD}"

  PUBKEY=$(node -e 'const c = require("./src-tauri/tauri.conf.json"); process.stdout.write((c.plugins?.updater?.pubkey || "").trim())')
  if [ -z "$PUBKEY" ] || [ "$PUBKEY" = "REPLACE_WITH_UPDATER_PUBLIC_KEY" ]; then
    echo "Updater pubkey is not configured in src-tauri/tauri.conf.json." >&2
    echo "Generate it with: npm run tauri signer generate -- -w ~/.tauri/type-updater.key" >&2
    echo "Then paste ~/.tauri/type-updater.key.pub into plugins.updater.pubkey and commit it." >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  if ! printf '%s' "$PUBKEY" | grep -Eq '^[A-Za-z0-9+/=]+$'; then
    echo "Updater pubkey in src-tauri/tauri.conf.json is not valid base64." >&2
    echo "Paste the full single-line contents of ~/.tauri/type-updater.key.pub." >&2
    exit 1
  fi

  echo "==> Building desktop bundle (.dmg + updater)"
  # macOS updater artifacts are produced from the `app` bundle target when
  # `bundle.createUpdaterArtifacts` is enabled. Building only `dmg` creates the
  # installer but not `Type.app.tar.gz` / `.sig`.
  npm run tauri build -- --bundles app,dmg

  DMG=$(find src-tauri/target/release/bundle/dmg -name "*.dmg" | head -1)
  TARGZ=$(find src-tauri/target/release/bundle/macos -name "*.app.tar.gz" | head -1)
  SIG_FILE="$TARGZ.sig"

  if [ -z "$DMG" ] || [ -z "$TARGZ" ] || [ ! -f "$SIG_FILE" ]; then
    echo "Build artifacts not found (dmg/tar.gz/sig). Aborting." >&2
    exit 1
  fi

  SIGNATURE=$(cat "$SIG_FILE")
  PUB_DATE=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)

  # latest.json is what the in-app updater reads. tauri-action generates this in
  # CI; locally we assemble it ourselves.
  cat > latest.json <<JSON
{
  "version": "$VERSION",
  "notes": "Release $TAG",
  "pub_date": "$PUB_DATE",
  "platforms": {
    "darwin-aarch64": {
      "signature": "$SIGNATURE",
      "url": "https://github.com/$REPO/releases/download/$TAG/$(basename "$TARGZ")"
    }
  }
}
JSON

  echo "==> Creating GitHub Release $TAG and uploading assets"
  gh release create "$TAG" "$DMG" "$TARGZ" latest.json \
    --repo "$REPO" \
    --title "Type $TAG" \
    --notes "Automated desktop release. Existing installs update in-app via Settings → Updates." \
    --latest

  rm -f latest.json
  echo "==> Desktop release published."
fi

if [ "$DO_IOS" = true ]; then
  echo "==> Building & uploading iOS to App Store Connect"
  # Reuses your existing native iOS build + push scripts.
  npm run ios:build
  npm run ios:push
  echo "==> iOS build uploaded to App Store Connect."
fi

echo "==> Done: $TAG"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Local release fallback — same outcome as the GitHub Actions Release workflow,
# but built on your own Mac. Use this once you exhaust the free macOS CI minutes,
# or any time you'd rather build locally.
#
# Usage:
#   scripts/release-local.sh <version> <desktop|ios|both>
#
# Examples:
#   scripts/release-local.sh 1.2.3 desktop
#   scripts/release-local.sh 1.2.4 both
#
# Prerequisites:
#   - Run on macOS.
#   - `gh auth login` done (used to create the GitHub Release for desktop).
#   - Desktop: TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY + TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD set
#     (see docs/RELEASING.md). The key is the one from `tauri signer generate`.
#   - iOS: Apple signing set up locally (same as your existing `npm run ios:build`).
set -euo pipefail

VERSION="${1:-}"
PLATFORMS="${2:-both}"
REPO="oogxdd/type_new"   # owner/name used in the updater download URLs

if [ -z "$VERSION" ]; then
  echo "usage: $0 <version> <desktop|ios|both>" >&2
  exit 1
fi

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
cd "$ROOT"

DO_DESKTOP=false
DO_IOS=false
case "$PLATFORMS" in
  both)    DO_DESKTOP=true; DO_IOS=true ;;
  desktop) DO_DESKTOP=true ;;
  ios)     DO_IOS=true ;;
  *) echo "platform must be desktop | ios | both" >&2; exit 1 ;;
esac

TAG="v$VERSION"
echo "==> Releasing $TAG (desktop=$DO_DESKTOP ios=$DO_IOS)"

bash scripts/set-app-version.sh "$VERSION"

if [ "$DO_DESKTOP" = true ]; then
  : "${TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY:?set TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY (the updater private key)}"
  : "${TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD:?set TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD}"

  PUBKEY=$(node -e 'const c = require("./src-tauri/tauri.conf.json"); process.stdout.write((c.plugins?.updater?.pubkey || "").trim())')
  if [ -z "$PUBKEY" ] || [ "$PUBKEY" = "REPLACE_WITH_UPDATER_PUBLIC_KEY" ]; then
    echo "Updater pubkey is not configured in src-tauri/tauri.conf.json." >&2
    echo "Generate it with: npm run tauri signer generate -- -w ~/.tauri/type-updater.key" >&2
    echo "Then paste ~/.tauri/type-updater.key.pub into plugins.updater.pubkey and commit it." >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  if ! printf '%s' "$PUBKEY" | grep -Eq '^[A-Za-z0-9+/=]+$'; then
    echo "Updater pubkey in src-tauri/tauri.conf.json is not valid base64." >&2
    echo "Paste the full single-line contents of ~/.tauri/type-updater.key.pub." >&2
    exit 1
  fi

  echo "==> Building desktop bundle (.dmg + updater)"
  # macOS updater artifacts are produced from the `app` bundle target when
  # `bundle.createUpdaterArtifacts` is enabled. Building only `dmg` creates the
  # installer but not `Type.app.tar.gz` / `.sig`.
  npm run tauri build -- --bundles app,dmg

  DMG=$(find src-tauri/target/release/bundle/dmg -name "*.dmg" | head -1)
  TARGZ=$(find src-tauri/target/release/bundle/macos -name "*.app.tar.gz" | head -1)
  SIG_FILE="$TARGZ.sig"

  if [ -z "$DMG" ] || [ -z "$TARGZ" ] || [ ! -f "$SIG_FILE" ]; then
    echo "Build artifacts not found (dmg/tar.gz/sig). Aborting." >&2
    exit 1
  fi

  SIGNATURE=$(cat "$SIG_FILE")
  PUB_DATE=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)

  # latest.json is what the in-app updater reads. tauri-action generates this in
  # CI; locally we assemble it ourselves.
  cat > latest.json <<JSON
{
  "version": "$VERSION",
  "notes": "Release $TAG",
  "pub_date": "$PUB_DATE",
  "platforms": {
    "darwin-aarch64": {
      "signature": "$SIGNATURE",
      "url": "https://github.com/$REPO/releases/download/$TAG/$(basename "$TARGZ")"
    }
  }
}
JSON

  echo "==> Creating GitHub Release $TAG and uploading assets"
  gh release create "$TAG" "$DMG" "$TARGZ" latest.json \
    --repo "$REPO" \
    --title "Type $TAG" \
    --notes "Automated desktop release. Existing installs update in-app via Settings → Updates." \
    --latest

  rm -f latest.json
  echo "==> Desktop release published."
fi

if [ "$DO_IOS" = true ]; then
  echo "==> Building & uploading iOS to App Store Connect"
  # Reuses your existing native iOS build + push scripts.
  npm run ios:build
  npm run ios:push
  echo "==> iOS build uploaded to App Store Connect."
fi

echo "==> Done: $TAG"

content.content:
name: Release

# Tag-driven releases. The tag encodes both the version and which platform(s) to
# ship:
#   v1.2.3           -> desktop (.dmg + updater) AND iOS (App Store)
#   v1.2.3-desktop   -> desktop only
#   v1.2.3-ios       -> iOS only
#
# You can also trigger manually from the Actions tab (workflow_dispatch) and pick
# the version + platforms there — handy for re-running a build without a new tag.
on:
  push:
    tags:
      - "v*"
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      version:
        description: "Version to release, e.g. 1.2.3"
        required: true
        type: string
      platforms:
        description: "Which platforms to build"
        required: true
        default: "both"
        type: choice
        options: [both, desktop, ios]

jobs:
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Parse the tag (or manual inputs) into a version + per-platform booleans.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  setup:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      version: ${{ steps.parse.outputs.version }}
      tag: ${{ steps.parse.outputs.tag }}
      desktop: ${{ steps.parse.outputs.desktop }}
      ios: ${{ steps.parse.outputs.ios }}
    steps:
      - id: parse
        run: |
          set -e
          if [ "${{ github.event_name }}" = "workflow_dispatch" ]; then
            VERSION="${{ inputs.version }}"
            SEL="${{ inputs.platforms }}"
            TAG="v$VERSION"
          else
            TAG="${{ github.ref_name }}"          # e.g. v1.2.3-ios
            BASE="${TAG#v}"                        # strip leading v
            case "$BASE" in
              *-ios)     VERSION="${BASE%-ios}";     SEL="ios" ;;
              *-desktop) VERSION="${BASE%-desktop}"; SEL="desktop" ;;
              *)         VERSION="$BASE";            SEL="both" ;;
            esac
          fi

          DESKTOP=false; IOS=false
          case "$SEL" in
            both)    DESKTOP=true; IOS=true ;;
            desktop) DESKTOP=true ;;

name: Release

# Tag-driven releases. The tag encodes both the version and which platform(s) to
# ship:
#   v1.2.3           -> desktop (.dmg + updater) AND iOS (App Store)
#   v1.2.3-desktop   -> desktop only
#   v1.2.3-ios       -> iOS only
#
# You can also trigger manually from the Actions tab (workflow_dispatch) and pick
# the version + platforms there — handy for re-running a build without a new tag.
on:
  push:
    tags:
      - "v*"
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      version:
        description: "Version to release, e.g. 1.2.3"
        required: true
        type: string
      platforms:
        description: "Which platforms to build"
        required: true
        default: "both"
        type: choice
        options: [both, desktop, ios]

jobs:
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Parse the tag (or manual inputs) into a version + per-platform booleans.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  setup:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      version: ${{ steps.parse.outputs.version }}
      tag: ${{ steps.parse.outputs.tag }}
      desktop: ${{ steps.parse.outputs.desktop }}
      ios: ${{ steps.parse.outputs.ios }}
    steps:
      - id: parse
        run: |
          set -e
          if [ "${{ github.event_name }}" = "workflow_dispatch" ]; then
            VERSION="${{ inputs.version }}"
            SEL="${{ inputs.platforms }}"
            TAG="v$VERSION"
          else
            TAG="${{ github.ref_name }}"          # e.g. v1.2.3-ios
            BASE="${TAG#v}"                        # strip leading v
            case "$BASE" in
              *-ios)     VERSION="${BASE%-ios}";     SEL="ios" ;;
              *-desktop) VERSION="${BASE%-desktop}"; SEL="desktop" ;;
              *)         VERSION="$BASE";            SEL="both" ;;
            esac
          fi

          DESKTOP=false; IOS=false
          case "$SEL" in
            both)    DESKTOP=true; IOS=true ;;
            desktop) DESKTOP=true ;;
            ios)     IOS=true ;;
            *) echo "Unknown platform selection: $SEL" >&2; exit 1 ;;
          esac

          {
            echo "version=$VERSION"
            echo "tag=$TAG"
            echo "desktop=$DESKTOP"
            echo "ios=$IOS"
          } >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "Release -> version=$VERSION tag=$TAG desktop=$DESKTOP ios=$IOS"

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Desktop (macOS): .dmg + updater artifacts, published as a GitHub Release.
  # tauri-action builds, signs the updater payload, generates latest.json, and
  # uploads everything to the release for this tag.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  desktop:
    needs: setup
    if: needs.setup.outputs.desktop == 'true'
    runs-on: macos-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20
          cache: npm

      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
      - uses: swatinem/rust-cache@v2

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm install

      - name: Set app version from tag
        working-directory: apps/desktop
        run: bash scripts/set-app-version.sh "${{ needs.setup.outputs.version }}"

      - name: Build, sign & publish desktop release
        uses: tauri-apps/tauri-action@v0
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          # Updater signing (required) — see docs/RELEASING.md.
          TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY: ${{ secrets.TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD }}
          # Apple notarization (optional — removes the Gatekeeper warning). Leave
          # unset to ship an unsigned .dmg (right-click → Open to launch).
          APPLE_CERTIFICATE: ${{ secrets.APPLE_CERTIFICATE }}

name: Release

# Tag-driven releases. The tag encodes both the version and which platform(s) to
# ship:
#   v1.2.3           -> desktop (.dmg + updater) AND iOS (App Store)
#   v1.2.3-desktop   -> desktop only
#   v1.2.3-ios       -> iOS only
#
# You can also trigger manually from the Actions tab (workflow_dispatch) and pick
# the version + platforms there — handy for re-running a build without a new tag.
on:
  push:
    tags:
      - "v*"
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      version:
        description: "Version to release, e.g. 1.2.3"
        required: true
        type: string
      platforms:
        description: "Which platforms to build"
        required: true
        default: "both"
        type: choice
        options: [both, desktop, ios]

jobs:
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Parse the tag (or manual inputs) into a version + per-platform booleans.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  setup:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      version: ${{ steps.parse.outputs.version }}
      tag: ${{ steps.parse.outputs.tag }}
      desktop: ${{ steps.parse.outputs.desktop }}
      ios: ${{ steps.parse.outputs.ios }}
    steps:
      - id: parse
        run: |
          set -e
          if [ "${{ github.event_name }}" = "workflow_dispatch" ]; then
            VERSION="${{ inputs.version }}"
            SEL="${{ inputs.platforms }}"
            TAG="v$VERSION"
          else
            TAG="${{ github.ref_name }}"          # e.g. v1.2.3-ios
            BASE="${TAG#v}"                        # strip leading v
            case "$BASE" in
              *-ios)     VERSION="${BASE%-ios}";     SEL="ios" ;;
              *-desktop) VERSION="${BASE%-desktop}"; SEL="desktop" ;;
              *)         VERSION="$BASE";            SEL="both" ;;
            esac
          fi

          DESKTOP=false; IOS=false
          case "$SEL" in
            both)    DESKTOP=true; IOS=true ;;
            desktop) DESKTOP=true ;;
            ios)     IOS=true ;;
            *) echo "Unknown platform selection: $SEL" >&2; exit 1 ;;
          esac

          {
            echo "version=$VERSION"
            echo "tag=$TAG"
            echo "desktop=$DESKTOP"
            echo "ios=$IOS"

          echo "Release -> version=$VERSION tag=$TAG desktop=$DESKTOP ios=$IOS"

          APPLE_CERTIFICATE: ${{ secrets.APPLE_CERTIFICATE }}
          APPLE_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.APPLE_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD }}
          APPLE_SIGNING_IDENTITY: ${{ secrets.APPLE_SIGNING_IDENTITY }}
          APPLE_ID: ${{ secrets.APPLE_ID }}

          APPLE_TEAM_ID: ${{ secrets.APPLE_TEAM_ID }}

content.content:
1	# Type
2	
3	A **local-first markdown notes app**. Your notes are plain `.md` files in a folder on
4	your own disk — no account, no lock-in, readable and editable by any other tool. Optional
5	Git sync keeps them in step across devices, including a one-button local-network server so
6	a phone can sync over Wi-Fi or a hotspot with **no external host**.
7	
8	Two apps share **one Rust core**:
9	
10	- **Desktop** — Tauri v2 + React 19/TypeScript (macOS, Windows, Linux; also the legacy Tauri-iOS build)
11	- **Mobile** — React Native (Expo), talking to the same core through UniFFI. Opens on a
12	  blank page you can type on immediately; swipe up files it away and gives you a fresh page.
13	
14	## Repository layout
15	
16	npm workspaces + one Cargo workspace:
17	
18	```
19	apps/desktop/          Tauri app (React frontend + src-tauri shell)
20	apps/mobile/           React Native app (Expo) — see apps/mobile/README.md
21	crates/type-core/      Framework-free Rust core (notes, git sync, recordings,
22	                       transcription queues, security, working folders)
23	crates/type-ffi/       UniFFI bindings over type-core for the mobile app
24	packages/shared/       @typenotes/shared — platform-free TS used by both apps
25	packages/mobile-core/  @typenotes/mobile-core — typed TS bridge to type-ffi
26	```
27	
28	## Highlights
29	
30	- **Plain-file storage** — notes are `.md` files in a folder tree you can point anywhere; order persists per folder.
31	- **Rich markdown editor** (Tiptap) with debounced autosave and content-based auto-naming.
32	- **Git sync** over `https://`, `ssh://`, or `git://` — push/pull across devices via libgit2 (no shell `git` needed).
33	- **One-button local sync** — host a `git daemon` on the desktop; the phone finds it by mDNS or QR code, no typing.
34	- **SSH key auth** — generate an Ed25519 keypair in-app for passwordless SSH.
35	- **Never-blocked merges** — conflicts keep your version and drop the remote copy beside it as `.conflict.md`.
36	- **Audio recording + transcription** — zero-install local Whisper on desktop, AssemblyAI on iOS.
37	- **Handwriting OCR** — import an image, get text back (OpenAI / Hugging Face).
38	- **Processing queues** — voice transcription and handwriting OCR run as separate queues with shared status plumbing.
39	- **Multi-profile** — independent notes roots and sync settings.
40	- **Extension surfaces** — multi-note lens and note encryption/lock/panic are kept behind a typed frontend registry.
41	- **Desktop & mobile UIs** — resizable three-pane on desktop; native-feeling stack/split navigation on phone/tablet.
42	
43	## Tech stack & architecture
44	
45	- **Frontend** — React 19, TypeScript, Vite, Zustand, Tiptap, DnD Kit, Tailwind +
46	  shadcn/ui. Feature-sliced domains feed separate desktop and mobile composition shells.
47	  Feature-sliced under `src/`: `app/` (composition root), `shared/` (domain-agnostic
48	  building blocks), `features/<domain>/`, optional `features/extensions/`, shared
49	  queue plumbing under `features/processing/`, plus thin `desktop/` and `mobile/` shells.
50	  Context providers are intentionally slim: state/action/workflow hooks carry the notes tree,
51	  profile, git sync, processing, command palette, and desktop editor/navigation workflows.
52	  Optional surfaces such as multi-note lens are extension-gated and lazy-loaded where possible.
53	- **Backend** — Tauri v2 (Rust) in a pragmatic **domain / application / ports / adapters / commands**
54	  layout, so use cases can move to another shell (e.g. UniFFI for React Native) without a rewrite.
55	
56	For the full module map and conventions see **[AGENTS.md](./AGENTS.md)**; for the Tauri
57	shell, **[apps/desktop/src-tauri/README.md](apps/desktop/src-tauri/README.md)**; for the
58	mobile app and its FFI bridge, **[apps/mobile/README.md](apps/mobile/README.md)** and
59	**[packages/mobile-core/README.md](packages/mobile-core/README.md)**.
60	
61	If you want a gentler architecture introduction in Russian, read
62	**[docs/architecture](docs/architecture/README.md)**.

64	## Quick start
65	
66	```bash
67	npm install                  # once, at the repo root (npm workspaces)
68	npm run desktop:dev          # desktop web dev server
69	npm run desktop:tauri dev    # desktop app
70	npm run mobile:start         # mobile (Expo; runs in demo mode without a native build)
71	```
72	
73	The mobile app runs against an in-memory mock core until the native module is
74	generated on a Mac (Rust cross-build + `uniffi-bindgen-react-native` codegen) —
75	see [apps/mobile/README.md](apps/mobile/README.md).
76	
77	### Isolated desktop dev
78	
79	If the production macOS app is installed on the same machine, use the isolated
80	dev flavor so development does not touch production app data (run inside
81	`apps/desktop/`):
82	
83	```bash
84	npm run tauri:dev:isolated -w type
85	```
86	
87	Production uses `com.digital.type2` and stores app data under
88	`~/Library/Application Support/com.digital.type2/`. The isolated dev flavor uses
89	`com.digital.type2.dev` and stores app data under
90	`~/Library/Application Support/com.digital.type2.dev/`.
91	
92	To build an isolated dev DMG:
93	
94	```bash
95	npm run tauri:build:dev -w type
96	```
97	
98	### iOS (Tauri build)
99	
100	```bash
101	npm run tauri:ios:init -w type    # one-time
102	npm run tauri:ios:dev -w type     # simulator/device
103	npm run tauri:ios:build -w type   # release
104	```
105	
106	### Build & checks
107	
108	```bash
109	npm run desktop:build    # tsc + web build + OTA fallback assets
110	cargo check --workspace
111	
112	npm run typecheck        # tsc --noEmit in every workspace
113	npm test                 # Vitest in every workspace (pure logic)
114	cargo test --workspace --lib   # Rust unit tests
115	```
116	
117	CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) runs the typecheck and both test suites on every
118	pull request and on pushes to `main`.
119	
120	Manual smoke checks:
121	
122	- **Desktop** — folder tree, note editing, DnD reorder, context menus, settings, keyboard shortcuts
123	- **Phone** — folders → notes → editor flow, back navigation, swipe actions, action sheets, sync
124	- **Tablet** — split view in portrait/landscape, rotation stability
125	
126	## Notes storage
127	
128	Notes live in a local folder tree. The app uses the first existing root:
129	
130	1. `NOTES_ROOT` environment variable
131	2. `./notes`
132	3. `../notes`
133	4. App-data fallback (`<app-data>/notes`)
134	
135	Each folder keeps its own `.notes-order.json` to persist the order of its child folders and
136	notes. A few system folders are maintained automatically inside every root: `Feed` (default
137	notes), `Archieve` (archive — the spelling is intentional and persisted), and the hidden
138	`Recordings/` (audio storage).
139	
140	## Security mode extension (encryption + lock + panic)
141	
142	The backend still contains note-body encryption, lock, and panic-reset support, but the
143	frontend treats this as an optional extension surface. Enable
144	`APP_EXTENSIONS.security` in `src/features/extensions/registry.ts` to show
145	**Settings → Security** and the lock screen in the app shell.
146	
147	- Note **body** content is encrypted at rest (XChaCha20-Poly1305 with an Argon2id-derived key).
148	- File names and frontmatter stay plaintext by design.
149	- The app launches **locked**, and backend content commands reject requests until you unlock.
150	- Lock manually anytime (`Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+L`, or **Lock now** in settings); optional auto-lock on background.
151	
152	Unlock vs. panic:
153	
154	- The **unlock** password decrypts notes and derives the in-memory data key (never persisted in plaintext).
155	- The **panic** password wipes local notes/profiles/settings/security state, seeds 3 dummy notes, and reloads.
156	
157	Notes:
158	
159	- Panic reset is local-only — it does not remove history from remote Git servers.
160	- Recording audio and attachments are not encrypted in this iteration.
161	
162	## Git sync
163	
164	The app uses embedded **libgit2** from Tauri commands — you do not need shell `git`.
165	
166	### What gets synced
167	
168	- All note markdown (`.md`), including recording notes. A recording is just a note whose
169	  frontmatter references its audio and tracks transcription state (`recording_audio_path`,
170	  `transcription_status`, `transcription_id`, `transcription_error`); the transcript text is
171	  written into the note body once it completes (no separate transcript file).
172	- Recording audio, stored flat in the hidden `Recordings/` folder as `Recordings/audio-<id>.<ext>`.
173	- Folder structure and every `.notes-order.json`.
174	
175	### One-time setup per device
176	
177	In **Settings → Profiles**, fill in:
178	
179	- **Remote URL** — `ssh://user@mac.local/path/to/repo.git`, `git://…`, or `https://…`
180	- **Branch** — usually `main`
181	- **Commit message** — the default auto-commit message for push
182	- **Username** / **Token/Password** — for HTTPS auth
183	
184	Then tap **Connect repo**, and **Push** (first device with notes) or **Pull** (to download
185	existing notes). Or just tap **Sync now** — it connects if needed, pushes local work, pulls
186	and merges remote changes, then pushes the result, in one step.
187	
188	### Three ways to sync
189	
190	1. **Remote repo** — point the Remote URL at any internet Git host (`https://…` or `ssh://…`) and **Sync now**.
191	2. **Local repo over SSH** — same Wi-Fi, more secure. Enable Remote Login on the computer, use
192	   the `ssh://` URL from the server card and the app's SSH key.
193	3. **Local repo over `git://`** — same Wi-Fi *or* your phone's hotspot. On desktop,
194	   **Settings → Sync → Local network server → Start server** spawns a `git daemon`. The phone
195	   connects with no typing: **Find on local network** (mDNS/Bonjour) or scan the desktop's
196	   **QR code**. Manual URL entry is the fallback. No internet and no external host required.
197	
198	See [docs/LOCAL_GIT_SERVER_LAN_HOTSPOT.md](docs/LOCAL_GIT_SERVER_LAN_HOTSPOT.md) for the
199	local-network flow.
200	
201	### SSH key auth (recommended)
202	
203	1. **Settings → SSH key → Generate SSH key**
204	2. Copy the public key into `~/.ssh/authorized_keys` on your server
205	3. Set the remote URL to `ssh://user@host/path/to/repo.git`
206	4. No username/password needed — the key authenticates
207	
208	Full guide incl. hardening: [docs/ssh-sync-setup.md](docs/ssh-sync-setup.md).
209	
210	### Pull / push & conflicts
211	
212	- **Pull** allows up-to-date and fast-forward updates. If you have uncommitted local changes,
213	  pull is blocked until you push/commit.
214	- **Diverged history** is auto-merged when possible. If the same file changed on both sides,
215	  your local copy is kept and the remote copy is saved beside it as `note.conflict.md`.
216	  **The merge always completes — sync is never blocked.** Both files are plain markdown;
217	  compare, edit the original, and delete the `.conflict.md` when done.
218	- **Push** auto-commits local changes with your message, then pushes.
219	
220	Typical loop: **Pull → edit → Push**. Across devices: Desktop edit → Push; iOS Pull → edit →
221	Push; Desktop Pull.
222	
223	### Security notes
224	
225	- Git username/token live in local storage on the device; the SSH private key lives in the app's sandboxed data dir.
226	- Sensitive fields are redacted from frontend invoke logs.
227	- Prefer least-privilege tokens; for SSH, restrict the key to git-only access (see the SSH guide).
228	
229	## Audio recording + transcription
230	
231	- Recordings are saved under `Recordings/` with a unique audio file each.
232	- Start/stop from the left panel (desktop) or the recording screen (mobile).
233	
234	### Desktop — local Whisper (faster-whisper)
235	
236	Desktop transcribes **locally** with [faster-whisper](https://github.com/SYSTRAN/faster-whisper)
237	— no API key, nothing leaves your machine, and **no manual setup**. The app provisions and
238	owns an isolated Python + faster-whisper environment under its app-data directory using
239	[`uv`](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) (it even fetches `uv` itself on first use). Open
240	**Settings → Recordings → Set up / Download model**, or just record — the first transcription
241	provisions automatically (the first run downloads the engine + model, so it can take a few
242	minutes).
243	
244	- Default model `large-v3`; change it in **Settings → Recordings** (`medium`, `small`, … or an absolute path to a local model).

246	- Check status, provision, or **Retranscribe** in **Settings → Recordings**.
247	
248	### Mobile — per-folder transcription mode
249	
250	Each working folder's `.type/settings.json` carries a `transcription_mode`
251	(set it in the mobile app's Settings → Transcription; it syncs with the notes):
252	
253	- **assemblyai** — transcribe right away on the phone via AssemblyAI (add your
254	  key in Settings; the key itself stays on the device).
255	- **desktop** — leave recordings pending; after a git sync your desktop's
256	  auto-queue transcribes them with local Whisper. Record on the phone,
257	  transcribe on the desktop, no cloud key needed.
258	- **native** — hook for an on-device speech recognizer, plugged in through the
259	  core's `TranscriptionProvider` FFI trait.
260	- **off** — never transcribe automatically.
261	
262	## OTA updates (iOS WebView assets)
263	
264	iOS web assets can be updated over-the-air via `@inkibra/tauri-plugin-ota`.
265	
266	```bash
267	cp .env.example .env     # then set VITE_OTA_MANIFEST_URL
268	```
269	
270	`npm run build` emits both the regular `index.html` assets and deterministic OTA fallback
271	assets (`dist/app.js`, `dist/app.css`). To prepare publishable artifacts + manifest:
272	
273	```bash
274	OTA_CDN_BASE_URL=https://your-cdn.example.com/type/ota npm run ota:prepare
275	```
276	
277	(`ota:prepare` also works without `OTA_CDN_BASE_URL` when `VITE_OTA_MANIFEST_URL` is set — the
278	base URL is inferred from `…/manifest.json`.) It writes `dist/ota/app-<version>.js`,
279	`dist/ota/app-<version>.css`, and `dist/ota/manifest.json` (with a SHA-256 hash). Point
280	`VITE_OTA_MANIFEST_URL` at that manifest.
281	
282	Flow: the splash bootstrap (`src/ota-bootstrap.ts`) calls `prepare(manifestUrl)` then
283	`start()`, which loads OTA content when available and otherwise the bundled `app.js` fallback;
284	startup is registered via `register()` in `src/main.tsx`. Users can disable startup OTA checks
285	in **Settings → Sync** (the app then skips the manifest fetch and starts bundled assets directly).
286	
287	## Mobile UX
288	
289	- **Phone** — stack navigation (Folders → Notes → Editor → Settings), back button + edge-swipe,
290	  long-press action sheets, swipe-left Archive/Delete, pull-to-refresh (refreshes tree + git status).
291	- **Tablet** — split view (folders/settings | notes/editor); portrait uses an adaptive split with stable content.
292	- **Editor** — save status line (Saving… / Saved / Save failed + Retry), 400 ms debounced
293	  autosave, guaranteed `flushSave()` on back navigation and app background/unload, and
294	  VisualViewport keyboard-inset handling.
295	
296	## Roadmap
297	
298	> Rough, early ideas — not yet designed or scheduled.
299	
300	- **Note "revisions" / multi-view notes (keep transcripts in the note, not in
301	  sidecar files).** Today the transcript result is already injected into the
302	  recording note's body, but everything still collapses into one flat body. The
303	  idea is to let a single note hold several distinct "revisions" (views/tabs),
304	  all stored inside the *same* markdown file — no separate files. For a
305	  recording that could be:
306	  - a. raw sentence/utterance-level transcript
307	  - b. the same transcript reformatted/cleaned up by an LLM
308	  - c. the user's own personal notes
309	  - d. anything else the user wants
310	
311	  This is **not recording-specific** — any note could expose extra views/tabs
312	  (e.g. the main note plus a side tab of related info the user types). The open
313	  questions are how to encode multiple views in one markdown file and how the
314	  editor surfaces them. Needs deeper design before any implementation.
315	
316	## Troubleshooting
317	
318	- **"Repository is not initialized. Connect a remote first."** — run **Connect repo** in Profiles settings.
319	- **"No matching Git credentials available…"** — check username/token for HTTPS, or generate an SSH key for SSH remotes.
320	- **Pull blocked by local changes** — push first, then pull.
321	- **SSH "Permission denied"** — ensure the public key is in `~/.ssh/authorized_keys` and the file is `chmod 600`.
322	- **SSH "Connection refused"** — enable Remote Login on the Mac (System Settings → General → Sharing).
323	
324	## Contributing
325	
326	Architecture, module map, and codebase patterns live in **[AGENTS.md](./AGENTS.md)**
327	(overview + both apps) and **[apps/desktop/src-tauri/README.md](apps/desktop/src-tauri/README.md)**
328	(Tauri shell). The shared Rust core (`crates/type-core`) is organized as
329	**domain / application / ports / adapters** across the `notes`, `profiles`, `security`,
330	`recordings`, `handwriting`, `import`, `git_sync`, and `local_sync` domains; the Tauri
331	shell adds `commands/` + the `platform` domain, and `crates/type-ffi` exposes the same
332	use cases to React Native.

# Type

A **local-first markdown notes app**. Your notes are plain `.md` files in a folder on
your own disk — no account, no lock-in, readable and editable by any other tool. Optional
Git sync keeps them in step across devices, including a one-button local-network server so
a phone can sync over Wi-Fi or a hotspot with **no external host**.

Two apps share **one Rust core**:

- **Desktop** — Tauri v2 + React 19/TypeScript (macOS, Windows, Linux; also the legacy Tauri-iOS build)
- **Mobile** — React Native (Expo), talking to the same core through UniFFI. Opens on a
  blank page you can type on immediately; swipe up files it away and gives you a fresh page.

## Repository layout

npm workspaces + one Cargo workspace:

```
apps/desktop/          Tauri app (React frontend + src-tauri shell)
apps/mobile/           React Native app (Expo) — see apps/mobile/README.md
crates/type-core/      Framework-free Rust core (notes, git sync, recordings,
                       transcription queues, security, working folders)
crates/type-ffi/       UniFFI bindings over type-core for the mobile app
packages/shared/       @typenotes/shared — platform-free TS used by both apps
packages/mobile-core/  @typenotes/mobile-core — typed TS bridge to type-ffi
```

## Highlights

- **Plain-file storage** — notes are `.md` files in a folder tree you can point anywhere; order persists per folder.
- **Rich markdown editor** (Tiptap) with debounced autosave and content-based auto-naming.
- **Git sync** over `https://`, `ssh://`, or `git://` — push/pull across devices via libgit2 (no shell `git` needed).
- **One-button local sync** — host a `git daemon` on the desktop; the phone finds it by mDNS or QR code, no typing.
- **SSH key auth** — generate an Ed25519 keypair in-app for passwordless SSH.
- **Never-blocked merges** — conflicts keep your version and drop the remote copy beside it as `.conflict.md`.
- **Audio recording + transcription** — zero-install local Whisper on desktop, AssemblyAI on iOS.
- **Handwriting OCR** — import an image, get text back (OpenAI / Hugging Face).
- **Processing queues** — voice transcription and handwriting OCR run as separate queues with shared status plumbing.
- **Multi-profile** — independent notes roots and sync settings.
- **Extension surfaces** — multi-note lens and note encryption/lock/panic are kept behind a typed frontend registry.
- **Desktop & mobile UIs** — resizable three-pane on desktop; native-feeling stack/split navigation on phone/tablet.

## Tech stack & architecture

- **Frontend** — React 19, TypeScript, Vite, Zustand, Tiptap, DnD Kit, Tailwind +
  shadcn/ui. Feature-sliced domains feed separate desktop and mobile composition shells.
  Feature-sliced under `src/`: `app/` (composition root), `shared/` (domain-agnostic
  building blocks), `features/<domain>/`, optional `features/extensions/`, shared
  queue plumbing under `features/processing/`, plus thin `desktop/` and `mobile/` shells.
  Context providers are intentionally slim: state/action/workflow hooks carry the notes tree,
  profile, git sync, processing, command palette, and desktop editor/navigation workflows.
  Optional surfaces such as multi-note lens are extension-gated and lazy-loaded where possible.
- **Backend** — Tauri v2 (Rust) in a pragmatic **domain / application / ports / adapters / commands**
  layout, so use cases can move to another shell (e.g. UniFFI for React Native) without a rewrite.

For the full module map and conventions see **[AGENTS.md](./AGENTS.md)**; for the Tauri
shell, **[apps/desktop/src-tauri/README.md](apps/desktop/src-tauri/README.md)**; for the
mobile app and its FFI bridge, **[apps/mobile/README.md](apps/mobile/README.md)** and
**[packages/mobile-core/README.md](packages/mobile-core/README.md)**.

If you want a gentler architecture introduction in Russian, read
**[docs/architecture](docs/architecture/README.md)**.

## Quick start

```bash
npm install                  # once, at the repo root (npm workspaces)
npm run desktop:dev          # desktop web dev server
npm run desktop:tauri dev    # desktop app
npm run mobile:start         # mobile (Expo; runs in demo mode without a native build)

minutes).

- Default model `large-v3`; change it in **Settings → Recordings** (`medium`, `small`, … or an absolute path to a local model).
- A background worker writes plain transcript text into the note body and word-level timestamps to `<audio-name>.transcription.json` beside the audio.
- Check status, provision, or **Retranscribe** in **Settings → Recordings**.

### Mobile — per-folder transcription mode

Each working folder's `.type/settings.json` carries a `transcription_mode`
(set it in the mobile app's Settings → Transcription; it syncs with the notes):

- **assemblyai** — transcribe right away on the phone via AssemblyAI (add your
  key in Settings; the key itself stays on the device).
- **desktop** — leave recordings pending; after a git sync your desktop's
  auto-queue transcribes them with local Whisper. Record on the phone,
  transcribe on the desktop, no cloud key needed.
- **native** — hook for an on-device speech recognizer, plugged in through the
  core's `TranscriptionProvider` FFI trait.
- **off** — never transcribe automatically.

## OTA updates (iOS WebView assets)

iOS web assets can be updated over-the-air via `@inkibra/tauri-plugin-ota`.

```bash
cp .env.example .env     # then set VITE_OTA_MANIFEST_URL
```

`npm run build` emits both the regular `index.html` assets and deterministic OTA fallback
assets (`dist/app.js`, `dist/app.css`). To prepare publishable artifacts + manifest:

```bash
OTA_CDN_BASE_URL=https://your-cdn.example.com/type/ota npm run ota:prepare
```

(`ota:prepare` also works without `OTA_CDN_BASE_URL` when `VITE_OTA_MANIFEST_URL` is set — the
base URL is inferred from `…/manifest.json`.) It writes `dist/ota/app-<version>.js`,
`dist/ota/app-<version>.css`, and `dist/ota/manifest.json` (with a SHA-256 hash). Point
`VITE_OTA_MANIFEST_URL` at that manifest.

Flow: the splash bootstrap (`src/ota-bootstrap.ts`) calls `prepare(manifestUrl)` then
`start()`, which loads OTA content when available and otherwise the bundled `app.js` fallback;
startup is registered via `register()` in `src/main.tsx`. Users can disable startup OTA checks
in **Settings → Sync** (the app then skips the manifest fetch and starts bundled assets directly).

## Mobile UX

- **Phone** — stack navigation (Folders → Notes → Editor → Settings), back button + edge-swipe,
  long-press action sheets, swipe-left Archive/Delete, pull-to-refresh (refreshes tree + git status).
- **Tablet** — split view (folders/settings | notes/editor); portrait uses an adaptive split with stable content.
- **Editor** — save status line (Saving… / Saved / Save failed + Retry), 400 ms debounced
  autosave, guaranteed `flushSave()` on back navigation and app background/unload, and
  VisualViewport keyboard-inset handling.

## Roadmap

> Rough, early ideas — not yet designed or scheduled.

- **Note "revisions" / multi-view notes (keep transcripts in the note, not in
  sidecar files).** Today the transcript result is already injected into the
  recording note's body, but everything still collapses into one flat body. The
  idea is to let a single note hold several distinct "revisions" (views/tabs),
  all stored inside the *same* markdown file — no separate files. For a
  recording that could be:
  - a. raw sentence/utterance-level transcript
  - b. the same transcript reformatted/cleaned up by an LLM
  - c. the user's own personal notes
  - d. anything else the user wants

  This is **not recording-specific** — any note could expose extra views/tabs
  (e.g. the main note plus a side tab of related info the user types). The open
  questions are how to encode multiple views in one markdown file and how the
  editor surfaces them. Needs deeper design before any implementation.

## Troubleshooting

- **"Repository is not initialized. Connect a remote first."** — run **Connect repo** in Profiles settings.
- **"No matching Git credentials available…"** — check username/token for HTTPS, or generate an SSH key for SSH remotes.
- **Pull blocked by local changes** — push first, then pull.
- **SSH "Permission denied"** — ensure the public key is in `~/.ssh/authorized_keys` and the file is `chmod 600`.
- **SSH "Connection refused"** — enable Remote Login on the Mac (System Settings → General → Sharing).

## Contributing

Architecture, module map, and codebase patterns live in **[AGENTS.md](./AGENTS.md)**
(overview + both apps) and **[apps/desktop/src-tauri/README.md](apps/desktop/src-tauri/README.md)**
(Tauri shell). The shared Rust core (`crates/type-core`) is organized as
**domain / application / ports / adapters** across the `notes`, `profiles`, `security`,
`recordings`, `handwriting`, `import`, `git_sync`, and `local_sync` domains; the Tauri
shell adds `commands/` + the `platform` domain, and `crates/type-ffi` exposes the same
use cases to React Native.

443	  functions per domain, JSON-string args/results matching the Tauri IPC
444	  shapes, so one set of TS wire types (`@typenotes/shared/types`) fits both
445	  shells. `init_core(app_data_dir, documents_dir)` must run first.
446	  `TranscriptionProvider` is a foreign trait (`with_foreign`): Swift/Kotlin/JS
447	  implementations run inside the core's queue worker.

449	  `setRawCore()` seam), `core-api.ts` (typed facade the app imports), and
450	  `mock-core.ts` (in-memory RawCore for vitest and "demo mode"). The real
451	  turbo module is generated on a Mac with `uniffi-bindgen-react-native`
452	  (ubrn 0.31.x = uniffi 0.31); output dirs are gitignored. Regenerate after
453	  any `type-ffi` change and keep `raw-core.ts` in sync.

455	  page (type immediately); swipe up files the page into Feed and a fresh
456	  blank page appears. `src/lib/capture.ts` (pure, tested) owns that note
457	  lifecycle with the same rules as the desktop editor (lazy create,
458	  debounced writes, flush on leave, empty-note cleanup). Screens: feed,
459	  folder browser, plain-text editor, record (expo-audio → `save_audio_recording`
460	  → queue per `transcription_mode`), sync (status/connect/pull/push/SSH
461	  key/history), settings (working folders, notes-root move, transcription
462	  mode, AssemblyAI key). Zustand stores in `src/state/`. Without the native
463	  module the app boots the mock core in demo mode (bottom banner) — that is
464	  what CI and Expo Go exercise.
465

467	
468	- **"Archieve" typo**: The archive folder is spelled "Archieve" in the codebase and in persisted data. Do not "fix" this — it would break existing user data.
469	- **Feed folder semantics**: `Feed` is the default notes folder and does not keep `.notes-order.json`.
470	- **Recordings storage**: audio files live under hidden `Recordings/`; notes created from recordings can be in `Feed` or the selected folder and reference audio via frontmatter.
471	- **Filename lifecycle**: per-profile setting controls new note file names:
472	  - `utc_timestamp_slug` (default): `YYYY-MM-DDTHH-mm-ssZ-<slug>.md`
473	  - `uuid_v7`: `<uuidv7>.md` (no auto-rename to slug)
474	  - `uuid_v7_prefix_slug`: `<uuidv7-prefix>-<slug>.md`
475	  New notes may start with placeholder suffixes (`-note-...`, `-recording-...`, etc.) and then auto-rename to content slug when enough text is available in slug-capable modes. Slug extraction is Unicode-aware (keeps Cyrillic/Latin letters and digits) and ignores `NV_EMPTY_LINE_TOKEN_*` noise.
476	- **Empty note cleanup**: if a dirty note is emptied and then focus/selection moves away, it is auto-deleted.
477	- **Per-folder transcription mode**: `.type/settings.json` inside a notes root carries `transcription_mode` (`off` / `desktop` / `assemblyai` / `native`). Absent = fall back to the legacy `mobile_auto_transcription_enabled` flag (true → assemblyai, false → desktop) — use `effective_transcription_mode()` / `effectiveTranscriptionMode()` instead of reading the field. Settings writers that omit the field must not clear a persisted mode (the core's `update_settings` merge handles this).
478	- **Two shells, one core**: new backend features go in `crates/type-core`, then get exposed twice — a `#[tauri::command]` in `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/` and a `#[uniffi::export]` in `crates/type-ffi`. After changing `type-ffi`, regenerate the mobile native module (Mac, ubrn) and keep `packages/mobile-core/src/raw-core.ts` in sync.

- **Per-folder transcription mode**: `.type/settings.json` inside a notes root carries `transcription_mode` (`off` / `desktop` / `assemblyai` / `native`). Absent = fall back to the legacy `mobile_auto_transcription_enabled` flag (true → assemblyai, false → desktop) — use `effective_transcription_mode()` / `effectiveTranscriptionMode()` instead of reading the field. Settings writers that omit the field must not clear a persisted mode (the core's `update_settings` merge handles this).
- **Two shells, one core**: new backend features go in `crates/type-core`, then get exposed twice — a `#[tauri::command]` in `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/` and a `#[uniffi::export]` in `crates/type-ffi`. After changing `type-ffi`, regenerate the mobile native module (Mac, ubrn) and keep `packages/mobile-core/src/raw-core.ts` in sync.

118	longer own workflows; their deeper persistence/worker logic remains in adapters.

129	- **handwriting** — a folder module (`handwriting/mod.rs` + `openai.rs` + `huggingface.rs`): save image attachment → note; `HANDWRITING_OCR_QUEUE` worker. `mod.rs` owns attachment saving, the queue + worker, note scanning, and provider dispatch; each provider's HTTP transcription lives in its own submodule — `openai.rs` (`HandwritingOcrProvider::OpenAi`, GPT-4o) and `huggingface.rs` (`::HuggingFace`, 503 retry). `collect_handwriting_notes`.
130	- **import** — Apple Notes folder importer. Walks an *exported* Apple Notes tree (Markdown/HTML/plain-text — Apple Notes has no native bulk export), creating notes in the active root. Auto-detects note files, converts HTML→Markdown best-effort, strips foreign front-matter, and preserves the original creation date (front-matter `created`/`created_ms`/… → epoch ms / RFC 3339 / date-only, else filesystem time). `preserve` mirrors the source hierarchy under one target folder; `flatten` drops everything into `Feed`. Runs on a worker thread writing to a process-global progress snapshot the UI polls (no Tauri events); `scan_apple_import_source`, `run_apple_notes_import`, `apple_import_snapshot`. Notes are written via `write_note_with_front_matter`, so encryption is transparent (import requires unlock).
131	- **git** (the `git_sync` domain) — libgit2 sync. `ensure_git_repo`/`open_repo`, `perform_fetch`/`fast_forward_to`/`merge_fetched_commit`/`commit_all_changes`, `resolve_target_branch`/`switch_or_prepare_branch`. Conflicts keep "ours" and write "theirs" as `.conflict.md` siblings — merge never blocks. `build_git_status`, `build_git_history`. `build_callbacks` auth order: app SSH key file → SSH agent → username/password. Ed25519 keypair under `<app_data_dir>/ssh/`. Bootstrap-artifact detection for first sync.
132	- **local_sync** — desktop hosts a `git daemon` over plain `git://` so a phone on the same Wi-Fi / hotspot can push/pull with no external host. Supervises the child in a process-global `Mutex<Option<RunningDaemon>>` (idempotent start, reaps dead handles, killed on app exit). `receive.denyCurrentBranch=updateInstead` lets phone pushes update the live working tree. Detects the outbound LAN IP via a connected UDP socket; advertises/browses the `_typenotes-sync._tcp` mDNS service for tap-to-discover. See `docs/LOCAL_SYNC.md`.
133	- **ios** (`#[cfg(target_os = "ios")]`, in the Tauri shell at `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/adapters/ios.rs`) — native AVAudioRecorder/AVAudioSession recording and WKWebView termination recovery via Objective-C interop. State in `IOS_NATIVE_RECORDER`, `IOS_WEBVIEW_TERMINATION_PROXIES`.
134	
135	### ports/ — contracts
136	
137	Each `ports/<domain>.rs` is documentation-first and now also carries
138	application-facing gateway traits. Public traits document the user-facing
139	contracts; `pub(crate)` gateway traits are what application services depend on.
140	Keep these in sync with adapter behavior when a contract changes.
141	
142	### Cross-domain dependencies & visibility
143	
144	```
145	lib.rs (shared utils) ← everything
146	profiles       ← security (panic reset, enable migration)
147	profiles       ← notes    (notes_root resolution)
148	notes          ← security (encrypt_note_body_for_write)
149	notes          ← recordings / handwriting (front matter, file naming, collection)
150	import         ← notes (root resolution, note creation/naming) + security (unlock gate)
151	git/local_sync ← notes (notes_root) + git helpers (repo/branch)
152	```
153	
154	Circular references (security↔notes, profiles↔notes) are fine — one crate, all
155	resolved via `crate::` paths. Symbols used outside their module are `pub(crate)`;
156	module-internal helpers stay private.
157	
158	## System folders and storage
159	
160	- Profile notes root is configurable per profile (`notes_root`). It can live in app data or any user-selected absolute path.

162	  - `Feed` — default notes folder

167	  - `Unsorted` -> `Feed`
168	  - `_Recordings` -> `Recordings`
169	- `Feed` does not keep `.notes-order.json`.
170	
171	## Security and encryption
172	
173	- Security config is persisted in app data as `.notes-security.json` (not inside notes roots).
174	- When encryption is enabled:
175	  - note **body** content is encrypted at rest (`XChaCha20-Poly1305` envelope)

177	  - app starts locked by default and backend content commands reject requests until unlock
178	- Password handling:
179	  - unlock + panic passwords are Argon2id-hashed
180	  - unlock password derives an in-memory data key (never persisted in plaintext)
181	- Panic flow:
182	  - entering panic password on lock screen triggers backend local wipe
183	  - notes/profile/security files are reset
184	  - backend seeds 3 dummy notes in `Feed`

186

188	
189	All paths in this section are inside **`apps/desktop/`**. Platform-free
190	helpers that used to live in `src/shared` (domain types, frontmatter,
191	note-preview parsing/format, annotation metadata, jobs, pure tree walkers,
192	system-folder constants) have moved to **`packages/shared`**
193	(`@typenotes/shared/<module>`) so the mobile app shares them; `src/shared`
194	keeps only browser-bound pieces (dom, storage/localStorage, base64 +

196	desktop-only constants).

- **notes** — a folder module (`notes/mod.rs` + `front_matter.rs` + `naming.rs` + `tree.rs`) for filesystem notes, front-matter, tree, ordering. `mod.rs` is the hub: shared constants (`ORDER_FILE`, `FEED_FOLDER`, `ARCHIEVE_FOLDER`, `RECORDINGS_STORAGE_FOLDER`, `ATTACHMENTS_STORAGE_FOLDER`, `PROTECTED_SYSTEM_FOLDERS`) + root/path resolution (`ensured_notes_root` resolves the active profile's root, `resolve_path`, `strip_root`) + concrete port adapters (`FilesystemNotesRepository`, `FrontMatterNoteDocumentCodec`, `RuntimeNoteBodyCrypto`, `UuidNoteIdGenerator`, `SystemNoteClock`). Note DTOs live in `domain/notes.rs`. `front_matter.rs`: `parse/render/write_note_with_front_matter`. `naming.rs`: `allocate_note_file_name` (UTC-slug / uuid_v7 / uuid_v7_prefix_slug) + Unicode-aware `slug_from_content`. `tree.rs`: `build_folder_node`, `ensure_system_folders`, `migrate_legacy_system_folders`, order helpers, `collect_markdown_note_files`.
- **profiles** — a folder module (`profiles/mod.rs` + `state.rs` + `settings.rs` + `backup.rs`) for multi-profile ("working folder") support. `settings.rs`: per-folder `.type/settings.json` (`ProfileSettings` — git remote/branch/credentials/commit message, legacy mobile auto flags, and the optional `transcription_mode` with `effective_transcription_mode()` fallback) plus the device-local `config.json` (`AppConfig` — API keys etc., never synced). `update_settings` preserves a persisted `transcription_mode` when an older writer omits it. `mod.rs`: `.notes-profiles.json` constants + DTO types + `profiles_file_path`/`profile_root_for_id`. `state.rs`: filesystem discovery, normalization, persistence, legacy `.notes-sessions.json` migration, and the `ensure_profiles_state`/`find_profile`/`*_state` CRUD (+ `normalize_notes_root_path`, dir copy/move helpers). `backup.rs`: profile backup zip + Documents export.
- **security** — XChaCha20-Poly1305 at-rest body encryption with an Argon2id-derived key. `SECURITY_RUNTIME` (OnceLock<Mutex>) holds the in-memory key after unlock. `.notes-security.json` config. `encrypt_note_body_for_write`, `decrypt_note_body_for_read`, `ensure_security_unlocked_for_app` (the lock gate most commands call), panic flow `panic_reset_local_data`.
- **recordings** — a folder module (`recordings/mod.rs` + `whisper.rs` + `assembly.rs`): save audio → note with metadata. `mod.rs` owns the transcription queue worker (which dispatches on `TranscriptionMethod`), types, queue state, note scanning, and file naming. Backends: `whisper.rs` (desktop, managed-Python `faster-whisper` via `whisper_env`; `check_whisper_availability`, `transcribe_audio_local_whisper`), `assembly.rs` (AssemblyAI cloud, used on mobile), and `TranscriptionMethod::Provider` — a shell-registered `ports::recordings::TranscriptionProvider` (how the mobile FFI plugs native speech recognition into the same queue). `queue_recordings_with_method` is the shared scan-and-enqueue; `collect_recording_notes`, queue snapshot for the UI. Native iOS capture lives in the Tauri shell's `TauriRecordingsAdapter`, not here.
- **whisper_env** — desktop only. Provisions and owns an isolated CPython + faster-whisper under app-data using [`uv`](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) (downloading `uv` itself on first use if absent), so the user installs nothing. `whisper_env_ready`, `managed_python`, `ensure_whisper_env`.
- **handwriting** — a folder module (`handwriting/mod.rs` + `openai.rs` + `huggingface.rs`): save image attachment → note; `HANDWRITING_OCR_QUEUE` worker. `mod.rs` owns attachment saving, the queue + worker, note scanning, and provider dispatch; each provider's HTTP transcription lives in its own submodule — `openai.rs` (`HandwritingOcrProvider::OpenAi`, GPT-4o) and `huggingface.rs` (`::HuggingFace`, 503 retry). `collect_handwriting_notes`.
- **import** — Apple Notes folder importer. Walks an *exported* Apple Notes tree (Markdown/HTML/plain-text — Apple Notes has no native bulk export), creating notes in the active root. Auto-detects note files, converts HTML→Markdown best-effort, strips foreign front-matter, and preserves the original creation date (front-matter `created`/`created_ms`/… → epoch ms / RFC 3339 / date-only, else filesystem time). `preserve` mirrors the source hierarchy under one target folder; `flatten` drops everything into `Feed`. Runs on a worker thread writing to a process-global progress snapshot the UI polls (no Tauri events); `scan_apple_import_source`, `run_apple_notes_import`, `apple_import_snapshot`. Notes are written via `write_note_with_front_matter`, so encryption is transparent (import requires unlock).
- **git** (the `git_sync` domain) — libgit2 sync. `ensure_git_repo`/`open_repo`, `perform_fetch`/`fast_forward_to`/`merge_fetched_commit`/`commit_all_changes`, `resolve_target_branch`/`switch_or_prepare_branch`. Conflicts keep "ours" and write "theirs" as `.conflict.md` siblings — merge never blocks. `build_git_status`, `build_git_history`. `build_callbacks` auth order: app SSH key file → SSH agent → username/password. Ed25519 keypair under `<app_data_dir>/ssh/`. Bootstrap-artifact detection for first sync.
- **local_sync** — desktop hosts a `git daemon` over plain `git://` so a phone on the same Wi-Fi / hotspot can push/pull with no external host. Supervises the child in a process-global `Mutex<Option<RunningDaemon>>` (idempotent start, reaps dead handles, killed on app exit). `receive.denyCurrentBranch=updateInstead` lets phone pushes update the live working tree. Detects the outbound LAN IP via a connected UDP socket; advertises/browses the `_typenotes-sync._tcp` mDNS service for tap-to-discover. See `docs/LOCAL_SYNC.md`.

### ports/ — contracts

Each `ports/<domain>.rs` is documentation-first and now also carries
application-facing gateway traits. Public traits document the user-facing
contracts; `pub(crate)` gateway traits are what application services depend on.
Keep these in sync with adapter behavior when a contract changes.

### Cross-domain dependencies & visibility

```
lib.rs (shared utils) ← everything
profiles       ← security (panic reset, enable migration)
profiles       ← notes    (notes_root resolution)
notes          ← security (encrypt_note_body_for_write)
notes          ← recordings / handwriting (front matter, file naming, collection)
import         ← notes (root resolution, note creation/naming) + security (unlock gate)
git/local_sync ← notes (notes_root) + git helpers (repo/branch)
```

module-internal helpers stay private.

- Profile notes root is configurable per profile (`notes_root`). It can live in app data or any user-selected absolute path.
- Required system folders inside each `notes_root`:

  - `Archieve` — archive folder (typo is intentional and persisted)
  - `Recordings` — audio file storage folder
- `Recordings` is hidden from folder tree/navigation and used as backend storage.
- Legacy migrations are handled by backend:
  - `Unsorted` -> `Feed`
  - `_Recordings` -> `Recordings`
- `Feed` does not keep `.notes-order.json`.

## Security and encryption

- Security config is persisted in app data as `.notes-security.json` (not inside notes roots).
- When encryption is enabled:
  - note **body** content is encrypted at rest (`XChaCha20-Poly1305` envelope)
  - filenames and frontmatter remain plaintext by design
  - app starts locked by default and backend content commands reject requests until unlock
- Password handling:
  - unlock + panic passwords are Argon2id-hashed
  - unlock password derives an in-memory data key (never persisted in plaintext)
- Panic flow:
  - entering panic password on lock screen triggers backend local wipe
  - notes/profile/security files are reset
  - backend seeds 3 dummy notes in `Feed`
  - frontend clears localStorage and reloads

## How the desktop frontend is structured

All paths in this section are inside **`apps/desktop/`**. Platform-free
helpers that used to live in `src/shared` (domain types, frontmatter,
note-preview parsing/format, annotation metadata, jobs, pure tree walkers,
system-folder constants) have moved to **`packages/shared`**

keeps only browser-bound pieces (dom, storage/localStorage, base64 +
yieldToUi, selection modifiers, shadcn `ui/`, the `invoke` wrapper, and
desktop-only constants).

1	# src-tauri — the desktop (Tauri) shell
2	
3	This crate is the **Tauri v2 shell** around the shared Rust core. Almost all
4	business logic — the **domain / application / ports / adapters** layers — lives
5	in [`crates/type-core`](../../../crates/type-core), which is framework-free and
6	also powers the mobile FFI ([`crates/type-ffi`](../../../crates/type-ffi),
7	UniFFI bindings consumed by the React Native app). What remains here is the
8	IPC transport and the platform pieces only a Tauri process can provide.
9	
10	## Directory layout
11	
12	```
13	src/
14	├── lib.rs              Crate root: app_env() (tauri::AppHandle → type_core::AppEnv),
15	│                       macOS window-alpha helpers, and the public run() entry point.
16	├── main.rs             Binary entry point (calls lib::run).
17	│
18	├── adapters/
19	│   ├── platform.rs     Native theme + file-export sheet (Tauri/objc APIs).
20	│   ├── recordings.rs   TauriRecordingsAdapter: wraps the core RecordingsAdapter
21	│   │                   and overrides the three native-capture methods on iOS.
22	│   └── ios.rs          (iOS only) AVAudioRecorder/AVAudioSession recording and
23	│                       WKWebView termination recovery via ObjC interop.
24	│
25	├── application/platform.rs   Platform use-case facade (the one domain that
26	├── ports/platform.rs         stays shell-side: theme + export sheet).
27	│
28	└── commands/           Thin #[tauri::command] wrappers, one file per domain.
29	    ├── mod.rs          App bootstrap (Tauri Builder, plugins, generate_handler!)
30	    │                   and the shared run_blocking_command helper.
31	    ├── security.rs     lock, unlock, enable, preferences, state.
32	    ├── platform.rs     native theme, file export sheet.
33	    ├── profiles.rs     profile CRUD, backup zip, Documents export, app config.
34	    ├── notes.rs        tree, read/create/write, meta, previews, move/delete/
35	    │                   rename, order, timestamps, markers.
36	    ├── recordings.rs   native recorder, save, transcription queues, list.
37	    ├── handwriting.rs  save attachment, OCR queue, list jobs.
38	    ├── import.rs       Apple Notes scan / start / status.
39	    ├── git_sync.rs     SSH keys, status, history, connect, pull, push.
40	    └── local_sync.rs   local git-daemon server, mDNS discovery.
41	```
42	
43	## How a command flows
44	
45	```
46	frontend invoke("read_note")
47	  → commands/notes.rs        (lock gate, arg structs — from type_core)
48	  → type_core::application   (use-case service, depends on port traits)
49	  → type_core::adapters      (filesystem, git2, crypto, HTTP, workers)
50	```
51	
52	Commands do not own business workflows. Each command file builds the relevant
53	`type_core` application service with the concrete core adapter, passing
54	`crate::app_env(&app)?` — the `AppEnv { app_data_dir, documents_dir }` seam
55	that replaced direct `tauri::AppHandle` usage when the core was extracted.
56	`ensure_security_unlocked_for_app` gates content commands while locked.
57	
58	The `generate_handler![]` macro in `commands/mod.rs` uses qualified paths
59	(`notes::read_note`, `git_sync::git_pull`, …) to disambiguate command modules.
60	
61	## What stays in the shell, and why
62	
63	| Piece | Reason |
64	|-------|--------|
65	| `commands/` | Tauri IPC is the transport; the FFI crate is the other transport over the same services. |
66	| `platform` domain | Native theming and the file-export sheet need the Tauri window / ObjC. |
67	| iOS native capture | AVAudioRecorder + WKWebView recovery need the app's ObjC runtime. |
68	| `app_env()` | Path resolution (`app_data_dir`, `documents_dir`) is the only thing the core needs from Tauri. |
69	
70	The "future UniFFI migration path" this README used to describe has happened:
71	`crates/type-ffi` exports the same use cases with `#[uniffi::export]` for the
72	React Native app. When adding a feature, put the logic in `type-core`, then
73	expose it twice — a thin command here, a thin export there.

content.content:
1	# Releasing — versioning, platform selection & CI
2	
3	This repo holds **one app** with two distribution targets that live on a **single
4	version line**: macOS desktop (Tauri, auto-updates in-app) and iOS (App Store +
5	OTA JS bundles). You can release **both at once, or just one platform** at a time.
6	
7	- The **git tag is the release trigger and the source of truth for the version.**
8	  You don't have to commit a version bump — tagging *is* the release. CI reads the
9	  version out of the tag and writes it into `package.json` + `tauri.conf.json`
10	  before building. (The version committed in the repo is just the dev baseline.)
11	- See also: [DESKTOP_AUTO_UPDATE.md](./DESKTOP_AUTO_UPDATE.md) for the desktop
12	  updater internals and one-time signing-key setup.
13	- For future Mac App Store / TestFlight releases, see
14	  [MACOS_APP_STORE_TESTFLIGHT.md](./MACOS_APP_STORE_TESTFLIGHT.md).
15	- For the local iOS/TestFlight upload flow, see
16	  [IOS_TESTFLIGHT_LOCAL.md](./IOS_TESTFLIGHT_LOCAL.md).
17	
18	---
19	
20	## 1. Versioning model
21	
22	**One monotonic version for the whole app.** Every release increments the number,
23	and the tag says which platform(s) ship. Numbers are not required to be contiguous
24	per platform — that's expected and fine:
25	
26	```
27	v0.5.0          both        desktop 0.5.0 + iOS 0.5.0
28	v0.5.1-desktop  desktop     desktop 0.5.1   (iOS stays on 0.5.0)
29	v0.5.2-ios      iOS         iOS 0.5.2       (desktop stays on 0.5.1)
30	v0.6.0          both        desktop 0.6.0 + iOS 0.6.0
31	```
32	
33	Each built artifact carries its own version baked in at build time, so a
34	platform that "skipped" a number is still internally consistent. The rule of
35	thumb: **bump the number on every release; pick the platform with the suffix.**
36	
37	### Tag conventions
38	
39	| Tag pattern        | Builds                          |
40	| ------------------ | ------------------------------- |
41	| `vX.Y.Z`           | **both** desktop + iOS          |
42	| `vX.Y.Z-desktop`   | desktop only (.dmg + updater)   |
43	| `vX.Y.Z-ios`       | iOS only (App Store)            |
44	
45	> Why this works for the desktop updater: the updater reads
46	> `…/releases/latest/download/latest.json`, so the desktop release must be
47	> GitHub's *latest* release. The workflow forces that for desktop/both releases
48	> and **never marks iOS-only releases as latest**, so an iOS release can't break
49	> the desktop update channel.
50	
51	### iOS has two release paths
52	
53	- **OTA (JS only)** — fast path for frontend-only changes. Push to `main` →
54	  `deploy-pages.yml` rebuilds the OTA bundle → the installed app fetches it. No
55	  App Store review, no tag needed.
56	- **Native (App Store)** — needed when Rust/native code or native deps change.
57	  This is the `-ios` / `both` tag path below.
58	
59	---
60	
61	## 2. How to cut a release
62	
63	### Option A — push a tag (normal path)
64	
65	```bash
66	git checkout main && git pull          # release from main
67	npm version 0.5.0 --no-git-tag-version  # optional: keep repo baseline in sync
68	git commit -am "Release 0.5.0" || true
69	
70	git tag v0.5.0                          # both platforms
71	#   git tag v0.5.0-desktop              # desktop only
72	#   git tag v0.5.0-ios                  # iOS only
73	git push origin v0.5.0
74	```
75	
76	CI ([`.github/workflows/release.yml`](../.github/workflows/release.yml)) parses
77	the tag and runs only the platform jobs it selects.
78	
79	### Option B — manual run (no tag)
80	
81	Actions tab → **Release** → **Run workflow** → enter version + pick
82	`both`/`desktop`/`ios`. Useful for re-running a failed build.
83	
84	### Option C — build locally (the free-tier fallback)
85	
86	GitHub's free macOS runners are limited (minutes reset monthly; macOS minutes
87	bill at 10× the included pool, so you get relatively few builds). When you run
88	out, build on your Mac with the **same result**:
89	
90	```bash
91	# desktop needs the updater signing key in the environment:
92	export TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY="$(cat ~/.tauri/type-updater.key)"
93	export TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD="<password>"
94	
95	scripts/release-local.sh 0.5.0 desktop   # or: ios | both
96	```
97	
98	It bumps the version, builds, signs, assembles `latest.json`, and creates the
99	GitHub Release via `gh` — exactly what CI does. (`gh auth login` required once.)
100	
101	---
102	
103	## 3. Required GitHub secrets
104	
105	Add under **Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions**.
106
